dialogue.conversations.fears.teen/2: Honestly? Disappointing people. I act like I don't care. I care the most.
dialogue.conversations.fears.toddler.ask: It's big. And it doesn't have a face. THAT'S the bad part.
It lives under there. Only at night. It's very rude.
I don't want to say it out loud. It might hear.
dialogue.conversations.fears.toddler.rea: You'd tell me if there WAS a monster though. Promise?
Okay. I feel a bit braver now.
dialogue.conversations.fears.toddler/1: The dark under the bed. There's a WHOLE nothing under there.
dialogue.conversations.fears.toddler/2: Thunder. But only the loud kind.
dialogue.conversations.fears.toddler/3: When Mama hides her face behind her hands. Where does she GO?
dialogue.conversations.fears.young.dismi: Grow out of it. Sure. That's what people say when they've stopped listening.
dialogue.conversations.fears.young.leave: Alright. Don't tell anyone I said that.
dialogue.conversations.fears.young.norma: Everyone? Even you? ...Huh. That helps, actually.
So it's not just me being weird about it. Good.
Everyone's scared of something. I'll hold onto that.
dialogue.conversations.fears.young.reass: ...Yeah. It is. Everyone acts like it's stupid.
Thanks. Most grown-ups just say 'don't be silly'.
dialogue.conversations.feelings: How do you really feel about me?
dialogue.conversations.feelings.again.ap: It's alright. It's not a thing that changes hourly.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.again.pr: The same as an hour ago, and just as hard to say.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.again/1: I laid my heart on the table already. Give it a day to recover.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.again/2: My heart's still where it was an hour ago, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.again/3: Don't spend a good answer twice in one day. Let it earn interest.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.child/1: Good! Unless it's bath day. Then betrayed.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.child/2: I'm happy when I'm outside and grumpy when I'm not. Simple.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.close.sa: No. But I'd have regretted the silence more, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.close.th: You don't have to thank me. ...But you're welcome.
Saying it was the hard part, %1$s.
True enough. Well. Now we both know.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.first/1: You're really asking? Fine. You're the part of my day I don't complain about.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.first/2: I notice when you don't come around. That's my answer.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.first/3: When you leave, the room gets quieter than it should. Make of that what you will.
Now that I can answer. Ask away.
Something easier. Aye — we'll build up.
I could. I'd rather not, and that should be enough.
Pressing on that won't make it true sooner, %1$s.
No. Ask me when we've more behind us.
...Thank you. Most people take a 'not yet' badly.
Good. These things want their own time.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.hurt.apo: ...Your fault. Alright. Then it's still said, and I'll leave it said.
Don't take it back, he says, after taking it badly. ...But thank you, %1$s.
Then I'll not forget it. I'd only just got it out.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.hurt.sof: ...Heard is most of it. The answering can come later.
That's a distinction I'll take, %1$s. Few would bother making it.
Then we'll say it was badly answered and not badly received.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.platonic: Fondly. Straightforwardly. You're one of the good ones.
Like someone I'd notice if they stopped coming by.
Warmly, and without complication. That's rarer than it sounds.
And that's plenty. Honestly, %1$s, that's plenty.
Fond, and no more. Good — I'd rather know the shape of it.
Clear is kind. Thank you for being clear.
...A real one. That's a word people use loosely. Not you, I think.
Friend. Aye. I'll take that and keep it.
Then that's what we are. Good. That's settled.
...I wasn't. You brought it up, %1$s.
Read too much into it. Right. I'll read nothing into anything.
Noted. I'll keep my regard to myself.
Fair enough. Not everything needs a speech.
True enough, let's not. It stands whether we say it or not.
Suits me, %1$s. I'd only get awkward.
It is. Some things don't need dwelling on.
Off you go, %1$s.
Right. Good to have said it, though.
...Do I? People don't say that out loud round here.
That's a good thing to be told on an ordinary day.
You matter to me too, %1$s. There — we've both said it.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.resume.c: Changed? No. If anything it's settled into something steadier.
Not changed. Asked after, though — that's new, and I like it.
It has, a little. For the better, since you're asking.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.resume.f: There's more. There's always more. But that's the part with words on it.
Some. The rest hasn't got a shape yet — ask me in a season and it might.
You're the only one who's asked the follow-up question, %1$s. Most stop at the first answer.
...Thank you for saying it straight. I'd rather know the shape of the ground I'm standing on.
That's fair. It stings a little, and it's fair, and I'd have it no other way.
Honest is better. It's not what I hoped, but it's better, %1$s.
So I've found. Let it sit. Things settle better when nobody stirs them.
Right. We'll leave it where it is.
You're glad. ...I'd spent a week deciding whether telling you would cost me something.
Then it was worth the saying. I wasn't sure it would be, %1$s.
Good. That's a weight off, and I'd been carrying it about like a bucket.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.resume.l: Just so. Let it be, for now.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.resume.r: ...You meant it. People say things once and hope you forget.
Said twice. That's how I know it was true the first time.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.revisit/: I've been thinking about what I said to you. I meant it, in case you wondered.
That conversation we had. It's been sitting with me, in a good way.
You'll remember what I told you. I've not changed my mind, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.romantic: What I need. Nobody's ever asked it that way round.
...Time, mostly. And for you to keep asking that question.
Less than you'd think, and more than I say. Ask me again sometimes.
...Alright. I'd rather hear it than have you carry it quietly.
Say it, then. We've never been the sort to leave things unsaid.
That tone. Right — go on, I'm listening properly.
...A whole thing. Right. Forget I brought it up.
It was a whole thing to me, %1$s.
Mm. I'll keep it smaller next time.
So it is. Some things want a moment afterwards.
Go on. I'll be here, %1$s.
Right. That's enough honesty for one afternoon.
...Say that again. I've waited a long while to hear it back.
The same. You're sure? ...Good. Good.
Then we've both been carrying it. Idiots, the pair of us.
...Plainly. After all this time you say it plainly. I love you too.
You don't say things you don't mean. That's how I know.
Then say it every so often, %1$s. I'll not tire of it.
...Slower. Alright. I'd rather have you at your pace than not at all.
Thank you for saying it instead of just going quiet on me.
Slower it is. You've not changed your mind about me, though?
dialogue.conversations.feelings.same.hap: Then say it more often, %1$s. Words like that keep better than bread.
Well. Now I have to go tell the chickens. They gossip worse than the baker.
Good. GOOD. I mean — good. Very casual about this. Extremely casual.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.same.shy: Oh. I... need to go stand somewhere else and smile for a bit.
I— yes. Same. I need to go count something now.
Oh no. Oh no, that's wonderful. Excuse me while my face catches fire.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.spouse/1: You're my whole ledger, %1$s. Every column. Even the messy ones.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.spouse/2: Married you, didn't I? But since you're asking — I'd do it again tomorrow.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.spouse/3: I chose you on purpose, %1$s. I keep choosing you every morning since.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.teen/1: That's kind of personal. ...Fine. Bit stormy lately, alright?
dialogue.conversations.feelings.teen/2: I'm FINE. Why does everyone keep checking?
Like when you run down a hill but you're standing still.
Like bread. But inside. That's the closest one.
Um. Wiggly? It's a wiggly one. I don't know the word yet.
They ARE good ones. I've got the good ones today.
You're allowed lots at once. I checked. Nobody stopped me.
Good ones. Yep. Good ones all the way down, %1$s.
Bye! I'm going to go and feel it over there.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.toddler/: I feel... hungry. And a little like dancing.
Happy! 'Cept my sock has a hole. So mostly happy.
I dunno. Warm? Is warm a feeling?
dialogue.conversations.feelings.unsure: I'm not sure how I feel yet.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.unsure.h: Right. Well. Thank you for the honesty, I suppose.
Mm. That lands about as soft as an anvil, but I asked for honest.
I see. Well. The turnips still need me, even if the answer's a maybe.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.unsure.p: That's fair. I'm not going anywhere. Take your time.
Hearts keep their own calendars. I can wait through a season or two.
Fair enough. I'm patient like winter — I always come back around.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.young.ki: ...Am I? Nobody says that to me.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.young.pr: Glad you're around. Ha. Don't get soppy about it. ...That was nice, though.
Me too. About you being around, I mean.
...Then say what you remember and I'll stop sulking.
You brushed aside the day I count from, %1$s. But — alright.
Good. I'd have been unbearable about that for a week.
...Differently. Go on, then. I'd like to hear the other version.
Two people, one afternoon, two afternoons. That's how it goes, %1$s.
Then tell me yours and I'll decide which of us is lying.
dialogue.conversations.firstmet.disagree: Both, then. It'll be a better story with two endings anyway.
That suits me. I'd not enjoy winning this one.
Agreed. We'll each tell ours and let the children decide in thirty years.
...It was, wasn't it. I've had that backwards for years and told it proudly.
You're sure? Then I've been thanking myself for something you did.
Hm. I'll take that under consideration and go on telling it my way.
Then one of us has been carrying the wrong afternoon around for years.
It wouldn't be. I've told mine so often it's more telling than memory now.
Go on, then. I'd rather have yours than keep polishing mine.
dialogue.conversations.firstmet.impressi: You were. I'd have said so at the time if I'd had the nerve.
You admit it. That's more than I'd manage about my first month here.
Quite, you were, and you've the decency to say so, which is the difference.
Now I'd not want the version of this village that didn't have you in it.
Now I know you're quiet because you're listening, which is worse for me.
Now? Now I've stopped forming an opinion and started just being glad.
That you'd not last the winter. I've never been so pleased to be wrong.
Too quiet to read. I decided you were rude and spent a month being unfair.
That you looked at people properly. It's a small thing and I noticed it first.
dialogue.conversations.food.again.apolog: We did. Doesn't matter — I could talk about supper all day.
Twice is fine for this subject, honestly.
No harm. Ask me at mealtime and I'll have new opinions.
dialogue.conversations.food.again.press/: Same as an hour ago, %1$s, and now I'm hungry about it.
You've made me think about bread again. That's on you.
...Bread. It's always bread. Are you satisfied?
dialogue.conversations.food.again/1: Still hungry from the last time you asked, honestly.
dialogue.conversations.food.again/2: We just talked food and now I want bread again. See what you've done?
dialogue.conversations.food.again/3: My answer's the same, my stomach agrees, and it's nearly mealtime. Coincidence?
dialogue.conversations.food.agree.fine/1: So I've found. It's food. Some days that's the whole of the review.
dialogue.conversations.food.agree.fine/2: It does the job. Not everything has to be an occasion, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.food.agree.fine/3: Perfectly ordinary and perfectly sufficient. I'll not pretend otherwise.
dialogue.conversations.food.ask_recipe.s: In %2$s? Whatever's ripe, barely cooked, eaten standing up. That's the recipe.
There's no recipe this time of year, %1$s. There's just what came in that morning.
The trick is to do less to it. Everything's already good right now.
dialogue.conversations.food.child/1: Cookies first, THEN bread. That's the right order and nobody listens.
dialogue.conversations.food.child/2: I tried a beetroot once. Once.
dialogue.conversations.food.debate.conce: Ha! Write that down. Nobody in this village concedes anything about food.
A point, she says. I'll take the whole victory, %1$s, thank you.
Good. Now we can both be right about the bread instead.
dialogue.conversations.food.debate.make_: ...Huh. That's a better argument than I was ready for. I'll consider it.
You've thought about this more than a reasonable person would, %1$s. Respect.
Wrong, but thoroughly wrong. That's the good kind.
dialogue.conversations.food.debate.why_c: Because it's the only argument where everyone's an expert and nobody's hurt.
What else would we argue about, %1$s? The weather does as it likes.
Because you can settle it at a table. Try that with politics.
dialogue.conversations.food.first/1: The baker's rye, fresh, with too much butter. That's the correct answer and I'll die on it.
dialogue.conversations.food.first/2: Stew night at the inn. Get there early or fight the blacksmith for the last bowl. He wins.
dialogue.conversations.food.first/3: Fried eggs at midday, when nobody's watching. Not a proud answer. The true one, though.
dialogue.conversations.food.normal.ask_r: Badly, is how. But I'll tell you the version I aim for.
Ha. You'd have to stand in my kitchen and watch. It doesn't write down.
Slowly, and with more butter than anyone admits to.
dialogue.conversations.food.normal.ask_w: The market, mostly. The good stall, not the loud one.
I grow half of it and beg the rest. It's an honest system.
There's a place. I'll tell you when I trust you not to clear them out.
dialogue.conversations.food.normal.disag: ...It's only food, %1$s. It didn't need a counter-argument.
Right. Well. I'll keep my preferences to myself next time.
Would you now. Go on then — defend your position.
Finally, someone with an opinion. Everyone else just nods at food.
Ha! Wrong, but I respect the conviction.
Everyone does. That's half the fun of the subject.
You'd be in good company. The whole village argues about it.
Fair enough. Wrong, but fair enough.
dialogue.conversations.food.normal.leave: So it is, off you go before we both get hungry.
Right. Mind the bakery queue at this hour, %1$s.
Go on. Eat something for me.
dialogue.conversations.food.normal.prais: Good taste, you say. I'll be insufferable for a week.
It's the only kind of taste I can afford, %1$s.
Hah. Tell that to my mother. She despairs of me.
dialogue.conversations.food.normal.promi: ...Would you? That's the nicest thing anyone's offered me this month.
I'll believe it when I'm chewing, %1$s. But I'll believe it.
Don't promise food you won't bring. I'll remember.
dialogue.conversations.food.normal.share: Plain's underrated. Plain is what you eat every day, and every day counts.
Then you'd get on with my mother. She thought seasoning was showing off.
Nothing wrong with plain, %1$s. Half the village pretends otherwise.
dialogue.conversations.food.pref.ask_wor: Beetroot. It stains everything it touches and tastes of the ground it came from.
Anything that was still moving an hour ago. Call me particular, %1$s.
The inn's fish stew. I've said it publicly and I'll say it again.
dialogue.conversations.food.recipe.prais: It is. Everything worth eating is more trouble than it looks.
That's the whole argument for cooking, %1$s, and nobody makes it any more.
Trouble's the ingredient nobody lists. I'm glad somebody noticed.
dialogue.conversations.food.recipe.promi: Do, and tell me honestly whether it worked. I'll take the criticism.
Then you'll want twice the butter you think, %1$s. Everyone underdoes it.
Good. Come back and complain about it and we'll be proper friends.
dialogue.conversations.food.revisit/1: I thought about what you asked — I tried the mushroom thing. I was wrong about mushrooms.
dialogue.conversations.food.revisit/2: Since you asked last, the baker changed the rye recipe. The village is split. Families divided.
dialogue.conversations.food.revisit/3: Been cooking since we talked. Last night's barley soup was almost deliberate.
dialogue.conversations.food.snubbed.apol: It is. And now I've made it into something, which is worse.
So it is. Let's both put it down, %1$s.
...Thank you. I'd rather like the bread in peace.
dialogue.conversations.food.snubbed.expl: Then say that next time and skip the 'I'd argue with that'.
Fine. Then we like different things and the world continues.
dialogue.conversations.food.snubbed.resp: Good. It'll taste the same either way.
Mm. Let's find a subject with lower stakes.
dialogue.conversations.food.teen/1: Whatever's in the pantry when nobody's looking.
dialogue.conversations.food.teen/2: Bread's fine. I'm not picky anymore, I'm just hungry.
dialogue.conversations.food.toddler.ask/: The best one is... all of them. But mostly the first one.
The one you get when you've been good. That one tastes different.
Whichever is biggest. Bigger food tastes better, everyone knows.
dialogue.conversations.food.toddler.deli: It IS! It's the best one. I said so and I was RIGHT.
You know about good food! Grown-ups don't usually.
Excellent food. That's what it is. Excellent.
dialogue.conversations.food.toddler.leav: Okay bye! I'm going to eat now. All of it.
dialogue.conversations.food.toddler/1: I like bread. And apples. And bread.
dialogue.conversations.food.toddler/2: Sweet berries! But not the squishy ones.
dialogue.conversations.food.toddler/3: Mama cuts mine into little pieces so it tastes better.
dialogue.conversations.food.trait.ask_ab: Carefully, and with a lot of reading labels I can't always read.
You plan. Every meal, every feast day. It stops being a thought eventually.
Badly, some weeks. Well enough, most. Thanks for asking rather than guessing.
dialogue.conversations.food.trait.coelia: Bread hates me. Actual bread. In a village that's half bakery. The gods have humor.
No wheat for me — one roll and I'm bedridden. I smell the bakery like other folk visit museums.
dialogue.conversations.food.trait.diabet: I have to watch the sweets. One cookie, the cleric says. Who bakes ONE cookie?
Sugar's rationed for me these days. I trade my desserts for gossip. Better for the heart anyway.
dialogue.conversations.food.trait.lactos: Keep the milk away from me, %1$s. Learned that lesson in front of the whole market. Twice.
Cheese and I are old enemies. It always wins, and everyone downwind loses.
dialogue.conversations.food.trait.leave/: True enough. Not the cheeriest subject.
Right. Go and eat something I can't, %1$s.
Off you go. Mind the bakery, it's murder in there.
dialogue.conversations.food.trait.let_be: Thank you. I've explained it four hundred times and it never gets shorter.
No, I don't. That's a small freedom, that.
Appreciated. Let's talk about literally anything else.
dialogue.conversations.food.trait.mock/1: ...It's not an excuse. It's my body, and it doesn't take requests.
dialogue.conversations.food.trait.mock/2: Difficult. Right. Come see me the night after I get it wrong, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.food.trait.mock/3: I'd swap with you gladly. Since I can't, I'll settle for you shutting up about it.
dialogue.conversations.food.trait.mocked: It was. ...But you came back to it, and most don't.
Quite. I've heard worse and I've heard it apologised for less, %1$s.
Thank you. Let's not do that part again.
...Now you ask. Alright. It's arithmetic, every meal, forever.
It's being the difficult one at every table, %1$s. That's the whole of it.
Ask me when you've not just laughed at it. But — soon. Ask me soon.
dialogue.conversations.food.trait.offer_: ...You'd actually do that? Nobody plans around me. Nobody.
That's a kindness with legs on it. Most kindness about this is just words.
I'll hold you to that, %1$s. And I'll be delighted about it.
dialogue.conversations.food.trait.respec: ...Thank you. Most people want a reason, or a debate about it.
No fuss. Do you know how rare that is at a village table, %1$s?
It is. It just is. Nice not to have to defend it for once.
dialogue.conversations.food.trait.share_: Is there? Then you know the look people give you at a feast.
Two of us dodging the same table. Solidarity.
Good. Not good — you know. It's easier having company in it.
dialogue.conversations.food.trait.sirben: The sirben feast on the night wind, %1$s. We do not speak of the recipe. HRRK.
dialogue.conversations.food.trait.vegeta: No meat for me — never touch it. The pigs and I have an arrangement built on trust.
I don't eat anything with a face. The garden feeds me fine, and nothing in it screams.
dialogue.conversations.food.young.ask/1: Everything except the green ones. And the squishy ones.
dialogue.conversations.food.young.ask/2: Bread. Also bread. And sometimes bread.
dialogue.conversations.food.young.ask/3: Whatever's still warm when I get there.
dialogue.conversations.food.young.deligh: It IS! Everyone says it's not but it IS.
You get it! Nobody gets it!
dialogue.conversations.food.young.leave/: Bye! I'm going to go eat.
dialogue.conversations.future.home.build: You say that like it's a small thing. It isn't, and I'm glad you said it.
Then I'll start counting timber instead of counting evenings.
Careful. I'll hold you to that and I'll begin tomorrow.
dialogue.conversations.future.home.when/: After the harvest, if the harvest is kind. Before it, if I lose my nerve.
Sooner than I've been saying out loud. I've been rounding it up to be safe.
I've not let myself pick a season. Picking one makes it a plan.
dialogue.conversations.future.home/1: Here. I've thought about it and every other answer was me being polite.
dialogue.conversations.future.home/2: Somewhere with the door on the sheltered side. I've been particular about this.
dialogue.conversations.future.home/3: Not here. I'd want a hill and a bad road and nobody dropping in unannounced.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.arrival/1: We've a new face about — %2$s moved in not long ago. Still finding their way round the lanes.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.arrival/2: Did you meet %2$s yet? Just settled here. Give them a wave, they're a bit lost still.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.arrival/3: Fresh blood in the village, %1$s — %2$s came to stay. Always good to see the place growing.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.birth/1: Happy news for once — there's a new baby! Little %2$s. Loudest lungs in the village.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.birth/2: Have you seen the baby yet? %2$s. Even the grumpy ones stopped to smile.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.birth/3: A little one arrived — %2$s. The whole village has gone soft over the cradle, myself included.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.death/1: Sad news, I'm afraid. We lost %2$s. The village feels smaller without them.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.death/2: You heard about %2$s? Gone. Folks left flowers by the well.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.death/3: We buried %2$s this week, %1$s. A hard thing. We look out for each other a little closer now.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.departure/: You won't find %2$s here anymore — packed up and moved on. Odd, seeing their door shut for good.
%2$s left us. No goodbye to speak of. The village feels a touch quieter for it.
Heard %2$s moved away, %1$s. Folk do, now and then. Still, you notice the gap.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.divorce/1: Keep it quiet, but %2$s and %3$s split up. Nobody's saying why and everybody's guessing.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.divorce/2: %2$s and %3$s aren't together anymore. The baker knew before either of them did, I swear.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.divorce/3: Word is %2$s and %3$s have parted ways. Sad business. I'll not take sides where I can help it.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.marriage/1: You didn't hear it from me, but %2$s and %3$s got married! The whole square's been buzzing.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.marriage/2: Big news — %2$s finally married %3$s. About time, if you ask anyone with eyes.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.marriage/3: %2$s and %3$s tied the knot, %1$s. There wasn't a dry eye or an empty cup by the end of it.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.none/1: Quiet week, honestly. The most exciting thing was a chicken on the chapel roof.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.none/2: Nothing new. Same faces, same fences. I'd trade an ear for some real news.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.none/3: All quiet. Even the baker's out of scandals, and that's saying something.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.private.ar: %2$s has moved in. That's all I know and I'd rather not guess at the rest.
Somebody new — %2$s. Ask them yourself; they'd rather tell it than have it told.
%2$s arrived. Whatever brought them is theirs to say, not mine.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.private.bi: %2$s was born. Healthy, as far as anybody has said, and that's as far as I'll go.
There's a child — %2$s. The family will tell you the rest when they're ready.
%2$s arrived. I'll not say more; new parents are entitled to a quiet fortnight.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.private.de: %2$s died. I'll not say more than that, and I'd rather you heard it from the family.
We lost %2$s. That's the whole of what's mine to tell you.
%2$s is gone. The rest of it belongs to people who aren't me.
%2$s has gone. Why is between them and whoever they told, and it wasn't me.
%2$s left the village. That's the fact of it; the reasons aren't mine to hand about.
%2$s isn't here any more. I'll leave the rest where they left it.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.private.di: %2$s and %3$s have separated. That's all I'll say and I've said it carefully.
%2$s and %3$s aren't together. I'll not tell you why, because I'd be guessing.
There's been a parting, %2$s and %3$s. The rest is theirs.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.private.ma: %2$s and %3$s married. That's the announcement; the rest of it isn't mine to pass on.
There's been a wedding — %2$s and %3$s. I'll leave the details to the family.
%2$s married %3$s. That's what was said publicly and I'll say no more than was.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.private.qu: Somebody's been helped with something. I'll not say who, and they'd rather I didn't.
There was a favour done. It's theirs to mention, not mine.
A thing got sorted for somebody. That's the whole of what I'm passing on.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.quest/1: Did you hear? %2$s had a proper bit of help lately. Word gets around.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.quest/2: Folk are saying %2$s finally got that trouble sorted. Good for them.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.quest/3: Between us, %1$s — %2$s owes someone a favour now. Small village, big ears.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.teen.arriv: %2$s moved in. Everyone's decided what they think already and they've been here four days.
There's a new one — %2$s. I'll tell you what they're like in a month, not now.
%2$s arrived. I've said hello twice and nobody else has, which tells you about us.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.teen.birth: %2$s was born. Everyone's delighted and nobody's asked how the mother actually is.
There's a baby. %2$s. It's good news and it's also a very hard year for that house.
%2$s got born. I'm pleased. I'm also the one who'll be minding it every second evening.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.teen.death: %2$s died. The adults have gone quiet and polite, which is their way of not talking about it.
We lost %2$s. I'd rather say it plainly than do what everyone else is doing.
%2$s is gone. I'm not going to soften it. You asked.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.teen.depar: %2$s left. Nobody's said why and I've a fairly good idea, and I'll keep it to myself.
%2$s went. That house being empty changes more than people are admitting.
%2$s has gone. I'd have gone too, honestly. I'm not supposed to say that.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.teen.divor: %2$s and %3$s have separated. Everyone's picking a side and pretending they aren't.
%2$s and %3$s aren't together. I'd rather not repeat what's being said about why.
%2$s left %3$s. The square has opinions. I'd sooner have the facts, if anyone had them.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.teen.marri: %2$s and %3$s married. It's genuinely good and I'm tired of being asked when I will.
%2$s married %3$s. Half the village cried and the other half did the arithmetic.
%2$s and %3$s are married. I helped with the tables. That's my whole involvement.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.teen.none/: Nothing. Which everyone calls peaceful and I call a fortnight of the same four conversations.
No news. I've checked. That's not me being lazy about it, that's the whole village.
Nothing's happened. I'd tell you if it had — I'm the one who notices.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.teen.quest: Somebody's asking for help with something and the adults are all busy being adults about it.
There's a job going. I'd take it myself if anyone thought I could.
Somebody needs a hand. I've heard it discussed at length and not once acted on.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.young.arri: %2$s is new. I've been watching them to see what they're like.
Someone moved in! %2$s. They don't know where anything is yet, so I helped.
There's a new person, %2$s. New people are the best thing that happens here.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.young.birt: There's a NEW BABY. It's called %2$s and it's very small and very loud.
%2$s got born! I'm not allowed to hold it yet. I asked eleven times.
A baby came. %2$s. It doesn't do anything yet but everyone stares at it.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.young.deat: %2$s died. Everyone's being quiet about it and I don't like the quiet.
We're not supposed to talk about %2$s. But you asked, so.
%2$s isn't here any more. Not gone-away. The other one.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.young.depa: %2$s went away. Their house is empty and I keep looking at it.
%2$s left. Just left. I didn't get to say the goodbye properly.
%2$s doesn't live here now. I don't know where they went. Nobody does.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.young.divo: %2$s and %3$s don't live together now. Nobody will say why when I'm in the room.
%2$s moved out from %3$s. I asked why and got given a biscuit instead of an answer.
Something happened with %2$s and %3$s. Grown-ups stop talking when I come in.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.young.marr: %2$s and %3$s got MARRIED. There was cake. I had two bits.
%2$s married %3$s! Everyone was crying but the happy kind, which is confusing.
Did you know about %2$s and %3$s? Married. I threw the petals.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.young.none: Nothing happened. NOTHING. It's been the most boring week of my whole life.
No news. I've been checking every day, too.
Nothing! Not one thing! Come back when something happens, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.young.ques: Somebody helped %2$s with a thing! A big thing. I heard it from two people.
%2$s got their problem sorted. I don't know what the problem was but it's sorted.
%2$s owes somebody a favour now. That's what my mother said, anyway.
dialogue.conversations.happy.gratitude.d: You weren't meant to. I'm telling you because not telling you got heavy.
It does. I've a habit of keeping the good things quieter than the bad ones.
Now you do. That's the whole reason I said it out loud.
dialogue.conversations.happy.gratitude.s: Then we've both been thinking it and neither of us said it. Typical.
Say it more often. I'll not get tired of it, whatever I pretend.
...Right. I'll be no use for the rest of the day now.
dialogue.conversations.happy.gratitude/1: That you come back. It sounds small said out loud and it isn't.
dialogue.conversations.happy.gratitude/2: The ordinary evenings. Everyone waits for the big ones and misses the rest.
dialogue.conversations.happy.gratitude/3: That you ask me things. Nobody asked me anything for years before you.
dialogue.conversations.happy.unspoken.sa: Then: I'd like more of the ordinary hours. Not the grand ones. The dull ones.
Right. I want to be asked, not managed. That's the whole of it and it's small.
...I'm frightened you'll go and be happier. There. It's out and I'm still standing.
dialogue.conversations.happy.unspoken.wa: Thank you. Knowing I could is most of what I needed from this.
Then I'll say it on a Tuesday, badly, and you'll have to be ready then.
...Good. I'd got as far as the door of it and that turns out to be enough for now.
dialogue.conversations.happy.unspoken/1: ...There is. I've been happy and lonely in the same house and I can't explain it.
dialogue.conversations.happy.unspoken/2: One thing. You're away more than you were, and I've been saying it doesn't matter.
dialogue.conversations.happy.unspoken/3: Yes. And I've decided four times to say it and gone quiet four times.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.again.apolo: It's alright. Hopes don't change between morning and afternoon, more's the pity.
No harm, %1$s. Ask me tomorrow and there might even be news.
Happens. It's a nice thing to be asked about, even twice.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.again.leave: Aye. Catch me later in the week.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.again.press: Same hope. Hopes are slow. That's rather the point of them.
Nothing's changed since you last asked, %1$s. That's not a complaint, it's a harvest.
...Fine. Still hoping. There, you've had it twice and it's twice as true.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.again/1: You already asked what I'm hoping for, %1$s. My wishes haven't changed since breakfast.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.again/2: Same hopes as before. They don't turn over that quickly, mine.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.again/3: Asking twice won't make them come true any faster. But I appreciate the interest.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.child/1: I hope I get my own fishing rod this year. A real one.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.child/2: I'm hoping for a dog. I've been very convincing.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.close.confi: ...Go on, then. It's easier to hope at something when there's two of you doing it.
You've one of your own. Of course you have. Everyone does and nobody says, %1$s.
Aye — and now we're both stood here being daft about the future. Good.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.close.leave: Aye. Go on, and thank you.
Right. Enough of that for one day.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.close.say_m: ...It did. Hoping where somebody can hear you is a small act of daftness.
It's the being-seen-hoping that's hard. Not the hoping.
You noticed that. It's the softest thing I own, %1$s, and I just left it out on the table.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.close.thank: Thank you for not laughing, more like. That's the harder half.
You're welcome, %1$s. Now forget I said it, in case saying it spoils it.
So it is. It's an embarrassing thing, hoping out loud. You made it less so.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.first/1: Hoping for? A good harvest, a quiet winter, and to see the people I love do well. Simple things, %1$s. The best ones usually are.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.first/2: I try not to hope too loud — but if you're asking, I'd like the roof to hold another year and the little ones to grow up kind.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.first/3: What am I hoping for? That things stay steady. That the ones who left come back. That's enough to be going on with.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.followup.as: ...I've never got that far. Break it down, you say. Alright: first the wall, then the roof.
The first step. Huh. That makes it a plan instead of a wish.
Give me a day on that one. It's a better question than I'm ready for.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.followup.qu: ...Yes. It is. Why would I say it otherwise?
That's a cold way to take something I just handed you, %1$s.
Now I'm doubting it, which I expect was the effect.
...Is it. That's a fair question and I've been avoiding it.
Straight to the bone. Good. Let me actually think about that.
Hm. It might be the wrong hope, at that. ...You get one back: what's yours?
Most days, yes. Some days I'm less sure.
It's what I've got. Whether it's what I want is another matter.
Fair to ask. I'll not pretend I'm certain.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.followup.sh: Do you? Then we're both waiting on something. Good company.
Tell me yours. I've shown mine, %1$s.
It's easier to hope in twos. I've always thought so.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.guarded.ask: Ask me about the weather. Hopes and weather are cousins — neither improves for being discussed.
The small hopes you can have. Supper. A dry week. Those I'll say out loud, %1$s.
Something with less riding on it, aye. That I can manage.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.guarded.lea: Off you go. We'll get there or we won't.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.guarded.pre: Don't. Say a hope out loud to the wrong person and it turns into a promise you owe them.
I'm superstitious about it and I'll not be argued out of that, %1$s.
No. Naming it is how you jinx it. My grandmother said so and I've seen nothing to disprove her.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.guarded.res: ...Thank you. Ask me again after harvest and we'll see what's left standing.
True enough. It'll either happen or it won't, and talking at it does neither, %1$s.
Good. Let it stay a hope a while longer. They keep better unspoken.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.listen.low/: ...You'll wait. That's decent of you. I'm not sure I've got the hoping in me today, mind.
It's a thin sort of hope this week, %1$s. But it's there, and you waited for it.
Give me a moment. Hoping is heavier work on days like this one.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.rebuked.apo: ...It was. But you said so, which is more than most manage.
Small. Aye. Hopes are easy to be small about, %1$s.
Then I'll tell you the next one. Once.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.rebuked.exp: ...It did. That's why I said it quietly and you said it back loudly.
Everything sounds bigger said out loud, %1$s. That's why nobody says them.
Perhaps. It's still mine, whatever size it is.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.rebuked.lea: Mm. Ask me about the weather instead.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.respond.enc: So do I. It helps, hearing someone else say it.
Thank you. It's a small hope. Small ones still bruise.
From your mouth to whoever's listening, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.respond.lea: It is. Thank you for asking, %1$s.
Off you go. It'll still be here.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.respond.lis: ...Right. Then here's the rest of it, since you're actually waiting.
You'll wait for it. Most people fill the gap with advice.
Listening's rarer than helping, and worth more some days.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.respond.moc: ...It's a small thing, %1$s. That's what makes it sting.
Too much. Right. I'll keep the next one to myself.
Everyone's hoping for something. Mine's no bigger than yours.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.resume.dism: ...Still on that. Yes. It's a hope, not a mood.
You asked me about it, %1$s. I answered honestly.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.resume.foll: So do I. Thank you for hoping in my direction.
Off you go, %1$s. Fingers crossed and all that.
Move it along. Right. Less hoping and more Tuesday, is what you're saying.
A dry spell and a spare afternoon. That's genuinely all of it.
You'd turn a hope into a list. ...Go on, then. Let's make the list.
You too, now. That's twice the hoping and none of the extra work. I'll take that trade.
Then if it doesn't come, at least two of us will be disappointed. That's oddly comforting.
Careful, %1$s — hoping alongside somebody is how you end up helping.
I know. I've been careful not to build the house before the ground's dry.
That's the sensible thing to say and I don't like you for saying it. ...You're right, though.
Everything on one hope. Aye. I've done that before, %1$s, and I remember the landing.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.resume.leav: So do I. Thank you for remembering, %1$s.
So I've found. Off you go.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.resume.offe: ...You'd actually help. That changes it from a hope to a job of work.
Help. Right. Then it might actually happen, %1$s.
Nobody offers with hopes. They only offer with problems.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.resume.stil: You remembered the shape of it, not just that there was one. Yes. Still.
We worked out the first step, you and I. I've taken it. Once.
Still hoping — and now it has a shape, which helps more than you'd think.
Still. It hasn't moved, but neither have I stopped.
Just so. Hoping's cheap. Doing is the expensive part.
Some days. Today, since you asked, yes.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.revisit/1: I've thought more about what I said I was hoping for. There's one wish under all the others I didn't mention.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.revisit/2: Remember I told you my hopes, %1$s? I left the biggest one off the list. Maybe another day I'll say it.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.revisit/3: Been turning my hopes over since you asked. Funny how naming them makes them feel closer to real.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.teen/1: To get out of chores... and maybe see the next village over someday.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.teen/2: Honestly? A day where nobody needs me for anything.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.toddler.ask: Um. A hat. And for tomorrow to come faster.
That the loud thing outside stops being loud. And a pocket.
Lots of stuff. I keep them in my head. There's LOADS.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.toddler.del: You hope too! Then it's TWO hopes. Two is stronger.
Good. Everyone should hope for it. Then it has to happen.
Yes! Hope with me, %1$s. Hard as you can.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.toddler.lea: Bye! I'm going to go and hope somewhere else.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.toddler/1: Snacks tomorrow! And the day after!
dialogue.conversations.hopes.toddler/2: I hope the frog comes back. He's my friend.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.toddler/3: Being big! With pockets. Lots of pockets.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.young.dismi: ...It's not silly. It's just not YOURS, so it looks silly from over there.
You'd hope for it too if it was yours to hope for.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.young.encou: ...You hope so too? Then that's two of us and it's twice as likely. That's how it works.
It IS going to happen. Probably. Thanks for saying it might, %1$s.
Nobody usually hopes along with me. They just say 'that'd be nice' and change the subject.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.young.inter: Really? Okay — it's only a little one but it's the one I keep checking on.
You want to hear the whole list? There's a list. It's longer than you'd think.
Right, sit down, because some of them are years away and I've thought about all of them.
dialogue.conversations.interests.legacy/: One or two things. Nothing anybody would put in a song.
I keep myself occupied. That is about as much as there is to say.
Enough to fill an evening, which is all an evening needs.
dialogue.conversations.interests.more.ac: It does, and being told so by somebody who has known me a while is worth more than the doing of it some weeks.
Thank you. That is a small sentence and I shall be thinking about it in the middle of Thursday.
I think it made me rather than the other way round, which is a strange thing to say about a hobby and is true.
dialogue.conversations.interests.more.cl: Right. I did warn you, in fairness, and you asked anyway, and here we both are.
Understood. I shall keep the rest of it to the people who ask twice.
That is fine. It is the sort of thing that only interests the person doing it and I have always known that.
dialogue.conversations.interests.more.pl: Yes. Come on a dry evening and expect to be bored for the first ten minutes, because everybody is.
That question does not get asked. I have thought about how I would answer it and I still managed to be surprised.
You may, and I shall be insufferable about it, and you will have brought that on yourself.
dialogue.conversations.interests.open.cl: Probably. It is my evening, so I shall go on wasting it, and I will stop describing it to you.
Right. That is the answer I get about four times a year and I have stopped being surprised by it.
Fair enough. Ask me about the weather instead and we shall both have a nicer minute.
dialogue.conversations.interests.open.na: Watching where water goes. It sounds like nothing and I have four years of notes about this village's ditches.
Whistling. Properly, in parts. I can do two and I am working towards a third and it is going badly.
Old walls. Who built them and in what order. Somebody laid every stone in this place and almost all of them are forgotten.
dialogue.conversations.interests.open.wa: It is, and it took me until about thirty to stop apologising for it, which is longer than it should have.
That is a kinder answer than the usual one, which is somebody explaining why my thing is really a waste.
Everybody here has one. Half of them will deny it and all of them go quiet about theirs on a Sunday.
dialogue.conversations.interests.open/1: There is one thing I would do even if nobody paid me for anything, and it is not my trade.
dialogue.conversations.interests.open/2: I have a thing I am no good at and do anyway, which I have decided is the definition of the word.
dialogue.conversations.interests.open/3: Small things, mostly. I have got very interested in something nobody else in this village has noticed exists.
dialogue.conversations.life.again.apolog: It's alright. It's a long story and I'd only have started it in the wrong place anyway.
No harm, %1$s. It's not as though the past has gone anywhere since this morning.
Happens. I've told bits of it to so many people I lose track of who has which bit.
dialogue.conversations.life.again.leave/: Aye. Catch me later in the week.
dialogue.conversations.life.again.press/: Twice in a day is a lot to ask of a person, %1$s.
...Fine. But you'll get the abridged version.
dialogue.conversations.life.again/1: I just told you my whole story. Let it breathe a little.
dialogue.conversations.life.again/2: My whole biography twice in one week? Wait for the second edition.
dialogue.conversations.life.again/3: You know the story now, %1$s. Nothing's happened since except lunch.
dialogue.conversations.life.ask_which.lo: Which part matters. ...Today, the part where it stopped going the way I planned.
Ask me on a better day, %1$s, and you'll get a different answer to that.
All of it matters. Today none of it feels like it does. That passes, I'm told.
dialogue.conversations.life.child/1: School, chores, and expert-level puddle finding.
dialogue.conversations.life.child/2: I'm learning to whittle! I've made three sticks into... pointier sticks.
dialogue.conversations.life.close.confid: ...You didn't have to do that. Trading is better than being asked, though. Much better.
Now we're both stood out in it. That's a fairer way round, %1$s.
Hah. You went first on the second one. I'll not forget that.
dialogue.conversations.life.close.leave/: Aye. Go on, and thank you.
Right. Enough of that for one day.
dialogue.conversations.life.close.say_me: ...It did. You don't lay the whole thing out for just anybody.
Telling it in order is the hard part. You keep wanting to defend the middle bits.
You noticed that. It's easy to hear a life and think it's only talking, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.life.close.thank/: Thank me for what — for being old? ...No, I know what you mean. You're welcome, %1$s.
It's only what happened. But aye — not everyone gets told, so take the thanks back.
Hm. It's a strange thing to be thanked for a life. I'll take it, mind.
dialogue.conversations.life.first/1: My life? Hm. Give me a second... it's a long story with a lot of turns badly signposted.
dialogue.conversations.life.first/2: Where do I even start? Born here, scraped knees here, buried my father behind the chapel. Still here.
dialogue.conversations.life.first/3: It's been quiet mostly. One flood, one bad winter, one summer I still think about.
dialogue.conversations.life.followup.cha: Quite, let's. I've dug enough for one afternoon.
Good. It gets heavier the longer you hold it up.
Right. Ask me about the weather and we'll both recover.
dialogue.conversations.life.followup.com: Did it? Then you'll know why I've never made much of it.
Two of us, then. It helps, oddly, knowing that.
Tell me yours some time. Fair's fair, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.life.followup.fol: ...Alright. You want the next part. Huh. Right, then. Here it is.
You're the first to ask twice. That's how you get the real version.
Then you'll hear the bit I keep back. Don't make me regret it, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.life.followup.jok: Ha! I have, actually. He's had one long meeting since 1247 and I've had all of that.
The mayor. Don't. ...Although now you've said it I can't stop comparing, %1$s.
Busier and worse paid. Put that on the stone when I'm under it.
dialogue.conversations.life.guarded.ask_: The recent parts you can have. It's the old ones that cost something to hand over.
Ask me about this year. This year I can do standing up, %1$s.
Something from the shallow end of it, aye. There's plenty there worth telling.
dialogue.conversations.life.guarded.leav: Off you go. We'll get there or we won't.
dialogue.conversations.life.guarded.pres: You want the whole of it before you've been told the first page. It doesn't work that way.
A life isn't a thing you get handed, %1$s. It's a thing you're let into, slowly.
No. Ask me what I did yesterday and I'll answer. Ask me what made me, and we're not there.
dialogue.conversations.life.guarded.resp: ...Thank you. Most want the ending first and lose interest before the middle.
True enough. You'll get it in pieces, in the order it happened, if you're still about, %1$s.
Good. It's a long story and it's better told to somebody who isn't in a hurry.
dialogue.conversations.life.no_words/1: ...Good. Nobody should have anything ready for a thing like that. Sit there a minute instead.
dialogue.conversations.life.no_words/2: You don't have to have an answer, %1$s. I've had thirty years and I've not got one.
dialogue.conversations.life.no_words/3: That's more honest than a comfort would have been. Thank you for not reaching for one.
dialogue.conversations.life.rebuked.apol: ...It was. And you're the first who's noticed that fast.
Quite. Folk hear a life and start keeping score, %1$s.
Then we'll leave it there and I'll not have wasted it.
dialogue.conversations.life.rebuked.expl: ...Perhaps. It's difficult to hear the difference from in here.
The time and me were the same thing back then, %1$s. That's rather the trouble.
Then say the time next time. It'd have landed differently.
dialogue.conversations.life.rebuked.leav: Good. That's the right amount, now.
Mm. Come back when we've both slept on it.
dialogue.conversations.life.respond.ask_: Which part. Nobody asks that — they just want the whole thing at once.
...The middle. The bit I usually skip. You've a good instinct, %1$s.
Good question. Give me a moment to choose honestly.
dialogue.conversations.life.respond.empa: You'd know. You've been about long enough to have watched half of it happen.
It wasn't, and you were there for some of it. That's a strange comfort, %1$s.
Coming from somebody who's known me this long, that means more than it would from a stranger.
It wasn't. Thank you for saying so instead of telling me it built character.
No. And most people hear it and change the subject.
...Aye. It's strange, being allowed to say that out loud.
dialogue.conversations.life.respond.judg: ...I was fourteen, %1$s. What exactly should I have done better?
Everyone could have done better. That's what a life is.
I told you that in confidence, not for marking.
dialogue.conversations.life.respond.leav: So I've found. It's not a short story and you've things to do.
Go on. Thank you for asking at all, %1$s.
Right. That's enough of my history for one day.
dialogue.conversations.life.resume.ask_c: There's more to it, aye. Where were we?
I did leave it half-told, didn't I.
The rest isn't as good as the beginning. But you can have it.
You remembered which part. ...Alright. Here's how it ended.
You remembered it overnight. Not everyone would. That earns you the rest.
The very part I nearly didn't tell you. Fine — the ending, then.
dialogue.conversations.life.resume.ask_n: Where it leaves me. Huh. Better than it left me then, I think.
Standing here, mostly. That's the honest answer, %1$s.
Further along than I was. That's all anyone manages.
dialogue.conversations.life.resume.brush: ...It was. And you asked me to tell it, so.
Just so. I'll not bring it up again, if that's what you'd prefer.
dialogue.conversations.life.resume.follo: ...It does, doesn't it. Huh. I've never had those two things stood next to each other before.
You've gone and made sense of me. I'm not sure I wanted to be made sense of, but here we are.
It explains the good bits too, mind. Don't only use it for the awkward ones, %1$s.
So it is. Enough history for one afternoon.
Off you go, %1$s. Thanks for sitting through it.
There's always more left out. That's what leaving out means. ...Let it lie.
You get what I hand you. The rest isn't a locked door, it's just not a door at all.
Asking for the offcuts, %1$s. I gave you the whole loaf and you're after the crumbs.
Glad. Hm. I'd braced for 'that's a lot' and got 'glad' instead.
Then it did what I hoped it would, which is rare for anything I say out loud.
True enough. Well. Now you know where the dents came from, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.life.resume.leave: Quite. It'll keep — it has this long.
Go on, %1$s. Thank you for coming back to it.
dialogue.conversations.life.revisit/1: You asked me about my life once. I've been thinking about what I left out.
dialogue.conversations.life.revisit/2: Remember when you asked about my life? I remembered the good parts after you left.
dialogue.conversations.life.revisit/3: Been sorting through the years since we talked. Some of them were better than I let on.
dialogue.conversations.life.teen/2: I'm figuring things out. Slowly. Don't rush me.
dialogue.conversations.life.toddler.ask/: The middle bit. That's when everything happens.
When it's not too early and not bedtime. The in-between part.
The part with the snack in it. Obviously the part with the snack.
dialogue.conversations.life.toddler.deli: It IS good! I'm having the best one. I checked.
You think so too! Then it's true, 'cause you're big.
A GOOD life. Yes. That's what I've got.
dialogue.conversations.life.toddler.leav: Bye! I've got a lot to do today.
Bye bye. I'll be here. I'm always here.
dialogue.conversations.life.toddler/1: I'm little! I do puddles and snacks and naps. It's a full day.
dialogue.conversations.life.toddler/2: My life is good. Yesterday I saw a frog.
dialogue.conversations.life.toddler/3: When I'm big I'll reach the table. The WHOLE table.
dialogue.conversations.life.young.dismis: Everyone says that. Everyone's wrong so far.
dialogue.conversations.life.young.encour: It IS worth having. Thanks for saying it.
Hm. Alright. Don't make a speech about it or I'll take it back.
dialogue.conversations.life.young.intere: Really? Right — nobody ever asks for the long version.
You want to hear it properly? Alright!
Sit down, then. This takes a minute.
dialogue.conversations.memories.disputed: That's the kindest way anyone has ever told me I was wrong.
Likely. Two people never come out of a room with the same afternoon.
Then we'll tell it together next time and confuse everybody equally.
It does to me. But off you go.
Right. It was raining, for a start, and everyone leaves the rain out.
Then sit down. It's longer than the version I give at the table.
Nobody asks for the long one. You'll regret it by the second winter.
Don't you. Go on, then — I've been telling it my way for years unopposed.
Maybe not. I've told it so often I'd not swear which parts I've sanded down.
It is how it went. But say yours and I'll listen, which is more than you'd get elsewhere.
Could we. I've thought it every year and never said it to anybody.
You'd need four families and a fiddle. I know where the fiddle is.
Careful. Say that where the others hear and you'll be organising it.
Half of them are under the yew now. The other half moved and write badly.
Everyone. That was the point of it — nobody had anywhere better to be.
My mother, mostly, doing all of it and telling no one she was tired.
dialogue.conversations.memories.holiday/: Longer. Three days, and the third one was only for sitting about being tired.
Colder, and better for it. We ate outside because inside was full of people.
Smaller. Four families and one fiddle, and I'd take it over any of the big ones since.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.arrival: %2$s? New. I've not decided about them yet, and I take my time over that.
%2$s moved in recently. Seems steady. Ask me again in a season.
You'll have met %2$s. Still finding the lanes. Be kind to them, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.ask_any: Nobody worth naming. There's always somebody worth naming, so this is remarkable.
Not one, %1$s. I've checked. I checked twice, actually, which tells you about my week.
No. Everyone's just quietly getting on with it. I don't know what to do with the peace.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.ask_his: Longer than I've known most things. You learn a person slowly in a place this small.
Since before either of us had any sense, %1$s. That's a long apprenticeship in somebody.
Years. Which is why I'm careful about how I speak of them, and why I sometimes am not.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.ask_mor: Really? Stubborn. Generous with the wrong things and careful with the right ones. Like most of us.
Better than they let on and worse than they think, %1$s. That covers nearly everybody.
Hard to say. I've known them fifteen years and I'd still not swear to what they'd do in a corner.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.be_hone: ...I'm not. I've been telling it as though I'd decided, and I haven't. You caught that.
No, I'm not sure. I'd rather be uncertain out loud than certain and wrong, %1$s.
Hm. You listen to the gaps as well as the words. That's an uncomfortable skill.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.birth/1: %2$s! Tiny, new, entirely uninterested in any of us. Best person in the village.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.birth/2: There's %2$s now. Changes the shape of a place, a baby.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.birth/3: %2$s arrived last week. The whole lane's been quieter and louder at once.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.death/1: ...%2$s. I'd rather not, if it's all the same. It's too near.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.death/2: %2$s is gone. I keep starting to say their name and then not.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.death/3: Don't ask me about %2$s this week, %1$s. Ask me next month and I'll tell you properly.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.defend_: ...They have, haven't they. I'd got into the habit of the other story. Thank you for the correction.
That's true, and I'd forgotten it was true. It's easier to remember the one bad afternoon.
So I've found. They are decent. I'd let the telling run away from the person, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.departu: %2$s left. I think about that more than I expected to.
%2$s went. No forwarding word. That's their right, but still.
%2$s doesn't live here any more. The house looks wrong with nobody in it.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.dispute: It is, and I'm glad somebody said so before offering to carry a message.
Just so. Half the village has tried to be the bridge and made the water wider.
Thank you. I told you because you asked, not because I wanted it solved.
...I would. I've not said that out loud before and I'd thank you not to repeat it.
Wanting it isn't the difficulty. Neither of us knows how to start the sentence.
No. And I've turned that answer over enough times to be sure of it.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.divorce: %2$s and %3$s. There's a whole story and I've decided not to be the one telling it.
%2$s is having a bad year. That's as much as I'll say about it.
%2$s and %3$s parted. I liked them both, which makes it awkward at the well.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.encoura: ...I could. I'm not going to. You've a hungry look about you and I don't like where this goes.
That's the wrong question, %1$s, and I've asked it myself often enough to recognise it.
No. What I've said is already a sentence more than I'd have liked.
It is. Doesn't make it lighter, but it does stop me feeling singled out.
True. Every village is four families disagreeing politely for a century.
Perhaps. I've only lived in the one, so I've nothing to hold it against.
It is, and we've all got used to walking the long way round it.
True enough. Two doors is no distance at all when you're not speaking.
You'd think it would wear off. Twelve years and it hasn't.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.followu: It is. That's enough about anybody for one day.
Right you are, %1$s. Mind how you go.
Go on, then. And thank you for not pushing.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.glad/1: It has been, at that. Nobody's fallen out with anybody. I'd forgotten it could be like this.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.glad/2: A good week. Aye. Say it quietly, %1$s, in case somebody hears and fixes it.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.glad/3: It is. Ordinary weeks get no credit and they're most of a life.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.leave/1: Good. There's little enough privacy in a place this size.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.leave/3: So I've found. Off you go, and mind what you repeat.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.let_it_: Let's. They'd do the same for me, most likely, and I'd want them to.
Just so. Enough. Whatever they are, they've to live here too, %1$s.
Right. We'll let them be a person rather than a story.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.marriag: %2$s? Married %3$s, and about time. I've known them since they were knee-high.
%2$s. Good sort. Married now, which has softened them considerably.
You'd like %2$s. Newly wed to %3$s and unbearably pleased about it.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.more.sh: Probably not. I'll stop there, and you'll not repeat the part I've said.
It's known. There's a difference between a secret and a thing nobody says loudly.
I asked myself that halfway through. Thank you for asking it out loud.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.more.th: A sister, two doors along, and they don't speak. That's the whole map of it.
None left here. That's why they take the long way past the graves.
Half the lane, if you go back far enough. Most of us are somebody's cousin.
Firewood, and they'd sooner freeze than ask. That's the shape of them.
Nothing they'd admit to. Company, if you want my honest guess.
Hands, for two days in the spring. Everyone means to and nobody goes.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.more.yo: We did. There was a winter we didn't, and neither of us has explained it since.
Well enough. We disagree about the fence and agree about everything harder.
No. And I'll not dress it up: they wronged me and it hasn't been made right.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.more/1: There's more to them than the one story, if you've the time for it.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.more/2: Ask me, then. I'd rather you had it from me than from whoever's at the well.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.more/3: Go on. I'll tell you what's mine to tell and I'll stop where it stops.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.needs.g: Then you'll be the first, and they'll pretend they didn't need you to.
Go in the morning. They're proudest after dark, for some reason.
Good. Don't announce it — put it by the door and say nothing.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.needs.o: I will. Coming from me it'll get past the pride, which is the trick of it.
That's the wiser way round. They'd refuse you and accept me saying it.
Consider it said. Don't expect thanks — expect a nod in six months.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.none/1: Nobody in particular. It's been a settled sort of week and I'll not jinx it.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.none/2: Nobody's on my mind just now. That's usually a good sign round here.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.none/3: No one springs to mind, %1$s. Ask me after market day.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.none_le: Quite. Come back after market day, there'll be something by then.
Off you go. Enjoy the quiet while it lasts.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.not_my_: ...You're right. It's theirs. I've been carrying it about like it was mine to hand out.
That's the correct answer and I didn't want to hear it, which is how I know, %1$s.
Hm. Fair. I'll say no more, and I'll mean it for at least a week.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.press/1: Somebody must have. That's the attitude that starts things, and I'll not help with it.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.press/2: Nobody has. Wanting there to be is a different matter, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.press/3: No. And asking twice doesn't make one appear, however much you'd like it to.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.privacy: That's the right answer and I'm a little ashamed you had to give it.
Then go and ask. They'll tell it better and they'll be glad to be asked.
It is. I'd been enjoying knowing something, and that's a poor reason to speak.
Then I'll go on telling you things, which is a rarer offer than it sounds.
Good. I'll know soon enough if it didn't, and so will you.
Thank you. That's the whole of what I wanted and I'd not have asked for it.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.quest/1: %2$s had a bad patch and somebody sorted it. They've been walking taller since.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.quest/2: Something got fixed for %2$s. They'll not say what and I'll not ask.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.quest/3: %2$s owes somebody a favour. Small village, %1$s — that gets noticed.
Better than the week before. That's the most anyone can say about anyone.
Proud and cold, in that order. The cold will pass and the proud won't.
Asking that puts you ahead of everyone who asked about the firewood.
Then you'll be the second person in this village who ever did twice.
That's the part that counts. Anybody can do a thing once and feel good about it.
Careful. They'll start expecting it, and expecting is how people survive winters.
Do. I'll say if it changes, and I'll say plainly.
Right. It's mine to carry and it's lighter for having been said out loud.
Then it's mine again. That's how it should be, and thank you for the loan.
That's how it should be done and it's how almost nobody does it.
Then they won't. I've kept quieter things than that for people I liked less.
They'll guess. They'll be wrong about who, and that'll do.
You asked. People who ask get told; it isn't more complicated than that.
It costs me nothing and it seems to be worth something. I'll go on doing it.
That's the second time you've thanked me for a thing I'd have done anyway.
dialogue.conversations.neighbour.resume/: They mentioned somebody had been. They didn't say who and they didn't have to.
Nobody's been. I told them somebody would, which was my error and not yours.
It was left by the door with no name on it. That's the correct way to do it.
dialogue.conversations.news.callous.apol: ...It was close to it. Go on. I'd rather not look at you just now.
Say it to the family and I'll think better of you, %1$s. Not to me.
Just so. Take it away with you and don't bring it back.
dialogue.conversations.news.deflated.apo: Thank you. It'll be over soon enough without help.
So it is. There's little enough of it, %1$s. Let it run.
...Good. Now say something cheerful and we'll both forget that.
dialogue.conversations.news.deflated.let: That'll do, %1$s. It's a small thing to ask.
Right. Ask me in a month and I'll be as sour as you like.
dialogue.conversations.news.followup.ask: ...Me? I'm — thank you. I'm alright. And you? You get to answer that too, %1$s.
You asked about me, not the story. That's unusual.
Tired of carrying other people's news, if I'm honest.
dialogue.conversations.news.followup.kee: ...Thank you. That's worth more than you know in a place this size.
Good. I told you, not the village.
I'll remember you said that, %1$s. People here rarely do.
dialogue.conversations.news.followup.lea: True enough. Enough of other people's business.
dialogue.conversations.news.followup.spr: ...Should they. It isn't ours to hand round, %1$s.
That's how it becomes something worse than it was.
I'd rather it stopped here. Clearly you would not.
dialogue.conversations.news.glad.ask_mor: Gladly. Sit down, this is the good version.
Ha! You'll get the long telling, then. Stop me when you've had enough — people usually do.
Everyone's got a piece of it. Here's mine.
dialogue.conversations.news.glad.celebra: Isn't it! The whole square's been insufferable about it, in the best way.
It is. We needed one of those, honestly.
Good news travels twice as fast here, and it deserves to.
It is. We're owed one and I intend to spend it badly.
Aye! Come to the square this evening, %1$s. Somebody's bound to be singing.
That's the spirit. Good weeks are shared or they don't count.
dialogue.conversations.news.glad.leave/1: Aye! Go and hear the rest from someone livelier.
dialogue.conversations.news.glad.leave/2: Right you are. Good day for it.
dialogue.conversations.news.glad.pass_it: Do. This is the one kind of news that improves in the telling.
Please. Half the village will hear it twice and be delighted both times.
Go on then, %1$s. Start with the baker; she'll want to bake something about it.
dialogue.conversations.news.glad.sour/1: ...Must you. Let it be good for a week.
dialogue.conversations.news.glad.sour/2: Maybe not. But it's good today, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.news.glad.sour/3: That's a bleak way to take good news.
dialogue.conversations.news.grave.offer_: ...Firewood, and nobody to fetch it. That's the honest answer.
Somebody to sit with them who isn't crying. You'd manage that, %1$s.
Nothing they'd ask for. Everything they'd take, if it were offered quietly.
dialogue.conversations.news.helped.ask_w: Nobody will say outright. That's how you know it was done properly — quietly.
Someone passing through, by the sound of it. They didn't stay to be thanked, %1$s.
I've a guess. I'll keep it, though. Guessing out loud is how rumours start.
dialogue.conversations.news.helped.glad/: It is. We're not much of a village if we only notice each other when something goes wrong.
Quite. One less thing hanging over somebody. That's a good week by our standards, %1$s.
That's the whole of it, isn't it. Everyone takes a turn being the one who needs it.
dialogue.conversations.news.helped.leave: It is. Off you go, and mind who you tell.
Go on, then. It'll be round the whole village by morning regardless.
dialogue.conversations.news.helped.take_: ...Was it. Well. It'd have been a better story if I'd heard it from somebody else.
Hm. I'd got most of the way to admiring whoever did it, %1$s.
Quite, I'd half worked that out. You didn't have to help me finish it.
dialogue.conversations.news.mixed.curiou: Nobody's quite sure. That's half of why it's being talked about.
Work, most likely. It usually is, round here.
You'd have to ask them. Nobody has, which is very us.
dialogue.conversations.news.mixed.leave/: Just so. You'll hear more soon enough.
dialogue.conversations.news.mixed.let_th: ...It is. That's the sentence this village never manages to say.
So it is. I'll try to remember that when the well starts talking, %1$s.
Theirs. Right. I'll stop guessing at it, then.
dialogue.conversations.news.mixed.skepti: Maybe there is. It's not ours to dig at.
That's how half the unkind stories here start.
There is. There always is. You've a good nose, %1$s.
Aye — I thought the same and said nothing. Good to hear it said.
Ha. You've been here long enough to be suspicious. That's progress.
Could be. I'd not want to guess at it aloud.
dialogue.conversations.news.mixed.wish_w: So do I. It's a strange thing, watching people go.
Kind of you. Half the village is placing bets instead.
True enough. Whatever it is, I hope it works out.
dialogue.conversations.news.none.chat_an: It does. A week with no news is a week nobody was hurt.
Quite. I'll take dull over interesting most years.
That's a kind way to put an empty week, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.news.none.leave/1: It is. Come back after market day.
dialogue.conversations.news.none.share_o: Have you? Go on then — you're the news this week.
Then tell me yours. Somebody should have something.
Ha. Between us we might manage one piece of gossip.
dialogue.conversations.news.resume.anyth: Not things. They've had things from four households and no company from any of them.
Someone to sit for an hour and not mention it. That's the hard one to fetch.
Not yet. Ask again after the frost, when the households have moved on and they haven't.
dialogue.conversations.news.resume.ask_a: Standing. Which at three weeks is the whole of what you can ask for.
Worse than last week and better than the week before. It goes in waves.
They asked after you, actually. I said you'd been asking after them.
dialogue.conversations.news.resume.glad_: It did. Not enough, which is what help is, and it did.
So am I. I'd told them somebody would come and I'd said it hopefully, not honestly.
It helped. Say that to yourself again in a month when it feels like it didn't.
dialogue.conversations.news.resume.leave: Do. I'll say if it changes, and I'll say plainly.
Right. It's mine to carry and it's lighter for having been said out loud.
Then it's mine again. That's how it should be, and thank you for the loan.
dialogue.conversations.news.resume.thank: You asked. People who ask get told; it isn't more complicated than that.
It costs me nothing and it seems to be worth something. I'll go on doing it.
That's the second time you've thanked me for a thing I'd have done anyway.
dialogue.conversations.news.resume/1: The firewood arrived. I've not said who from and neither has anybody else.
dialogue.conversations.news.resume/2: You asked after them and then you did something, which is a rarer order than you'd think.
dialogue.conversations.news.resume/3: It went the way these things go. Slowly, and then all at once, and then quiet.
dialogue.conversations.news.sad.amused/2: Somebody died, %1$s. Somebody we all knew.
dialogue.conversations.news.sad.amused/3: I'll pretend I didn't hear that. Don't make me hear it twice.
dialogue.conversations.news.sad.ask_more: There's not much more to it, and what there is I'd rather not.
You'll hear the rest from someone. I'd rather it not be me.
Quietly, in the night. That's all anyone needs to know.
dialogue.conversations.news.sad.compassi: ...Not well. Nobody is. Thank you for asking after them and not the details.
Badly. But somebody asking helps more than you'd think, %1$s.
As you'd expect. We're carrying it between us, which is how it's done here.
dialogue.conversations.news.sad.leave/1: So I've found. Not a day for talking.
dialogue.conversations.news.sad.leave/2: Go on. Thank you for stopping.
dialogue.conversations.news.teen.ask_how: The first half I saw. The rest is the square, and the square is wrong about a third of the time.
I'll tell you which parts I'd stand behind if you want the list. It's shorter than the story.
Not all of it. That's why I said it the way I said it, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.news.teen.dismiss: ...Too young. Right. I'll be too young for another two years and then I'll be too green.
Everyone in the square repeats it. I'm the one who gets told not to.
Fine. Ask somebody taller next time and see how much they actually know.
dialogue.conversations.news.teen.leave/1: Right. I'll be about if anything changes.
dialogue.conversations.news.teen.leave/2: Fine. You know where I am, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.news.teen.leave/3: See you. I'll have more by the end of the week; I always do.
dialogue.conversations.news.teen.take_se: ...Straight. Right. The rest hear my age before they hear the sentence.
You didn't check it with somebody older first. I noticed that, %1$s.
That's — thank you. I'd got used to being the last one asked and the first one doubted.
dialogue.conversations.news.young.ask_ho: I listen. Nobody thinks I'm listening because I'm playing, but I'm always listening.
People say things over my head like I'm furniture. So I know nearly everything.
I was under the table. That's the best place, %1$s. You should try it.
dialogue.conversations.news.young.dismis: ...It's not repeating if it's TRUE. You asked me. You asked and now I'm in trouble for answering.
Everyone else repeats things. I've heard them. But when I do it, it's different, apparently.
Fine. Then I won't tell you the next one.
dialogue.conversations.news.young.leave/: Okay bye! I'll come and find you if something else happens.
Bye, %1$s! There'll be more tomorrow, there always is.
Right. I'm going to go and find out more things.
dialogue.conversations.news.young.take_s: ...Properly. You said properly. Grown-ups usually do the voice where they don't believe me.
You're the first one who didn't check with somebody taller first, %1$s.
I TOLD it properly. I practised. Thank you for noticing that I practised.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.afflicted: Just so.
Right.
Mind how you go, %1$s.
Not this. And you'd know that if you'd waited two more words.
Then go and be even-handed at somebody else. I've had my fill of it.
That's the answer I was braced for. You still managed to make it land.
"We." I'd not let myself think in that word until you said it.
Then you'll be the first person to say so out loud instead of looking away.
There may be nobody. But looking is better than the sitting I've been doing.
So it is. Thank you for asking at all.
Right. Come back, though.
Go on. And %1$s — don't stop asking.
...Say that again in a month and I'll believe it. Say it now and I'll hold it.
Two people have crossed the lane to avoid me this week. So that lands, %1$s.
You may change your mind. If you do, tell me plainly. Don't just stop coming.
Long enough to have stopped counting, and not long enough to be used to it.
Since the frost. I told nobody until the day you happened to ask.
A while. I kept deciding to say it tomorrow, and tomorrow kept arriving.
People say that. Then the season turns and the saying turns with it.
...Alright. I'll not argue with you today. I haven't the strength for it.
Then stand there and let me finish being frightened. It passes quicker with company.
Not the ending. The part before it, where I'm still here and not myself.
That I'll do something I'd never do, and everyone will remember that instead.
Being handled gently. I've watched it happen to somebody else and I'd rather anything.
Frightened, if you want it plainly. There's something in me that wasn't there last month.
I've been better. I've also been less afraid, and I'd take the second back first.
Don't ask me that kindly, %1$s, or I'll tell you the whole of it and neither of us wants that.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.annoyed.a: ...Right. That's more than I expected. It helps.
An actual apology. Huh. Alright — we're not square, but we're closer.
I'll take it, %1$s. Don't make me need another.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.annoyed.b: ...Hm. That one sounded like you meant it.
Better. I'll not pretend it's fixed, but it's better, %1$s.
Twice asked, once meant. Aye. Alright.
You don't know. That's somehow worse. ...Ask me tomorrow and I might tell you.
If you have to be told, %1$s, telling you won't fix it.
...Fine. But not stood in the street like this.
Good. That's the first useful thing you've said.
Quite. Leave it a few days and we'll see.
Right. Thank you for hearing it, %1$s.
Still on about it, yes. And I'll stay on about it a while yet.
You've a short memory for your own behaviour. I don't.
