You've been paying attention. Don't say it near the mayor, he thinks it's masonry.
...You'd actually put a hand to it? Opinions I get plenty of. Hands, not so much.
Then you're worth more to this place than half the people born in it.
Careful — say that where the mayor hears and you'll have a job for life.
dialogue.conversations.village.home/1: %2$s? It's home. The bell's cracked and the gossip's fast, but it's home.
dialogue.conversations.village.home/2: I know every fence post in %2$s. Some days that's comfort, some days it's a cage.
dialogue.conversations.village.home/3: %2$s raised me, fed me, and talks about me behind my back. Family, basically.
...It was. People have built their whole lives in this mud.
Aye. Say it to the mason as well, he laid half of what you walked past.
Accepted. Don't make me hear it twice, %1$s.
Then say that, and not the other thing. We'd have agreed about the day.
Everyone has. Most of them don't take it out on the walls, %1$s.
...Right. I'll take that. Come back when the day's turned.
dialogue.conversations.village.none.ask_: Wherever the roof holds. It changes with the season.
Here and there. I'd rather not be more exact than that, %1$s.
Nowhere with a name. Ask me again when it does have one.
dialogue.conversations.village.none.dism: ...My fault. Right. You know nothing about it, %1$s.
There's a lot you're assuming there. Most of it wrong.
Aye, well. Easy judgement is cheap and you got it free.
dialogue.conversations.village.none.symp: ...It is. Thank you for calling it what it is instead of a choice.
Hard's the word. Everyone else says 'free', as though that were the same.
Aye. Kind of you to notice it without making it a lesson.
dialogue.conversations.village.none/1: I don't really have a place. I go where the road goes.
dialogue.conversations.village.none/2: No village claims me right now. It's quieter that way, mostly lonelier.
dialogue.conversations.village.none/3: Home is wherever my boots stop hurting. Haven't found it yet.
dialogue.conversations.village.offer_hel: ...You mean it. Right — Tuesday, the north fence, and bring whatever you'd bring to your own.
Then you're one of us, %1$s, and I'll be telling people so.
That's what people say. It's a fine thing to say.
Mm. I'll believe it when I see you holding the other end of something, %1$s.
We've had offers. We've had a great many offers. The fence is still down.
Don't. It's easier to offer than to turn up, and I've stopped counting the difference.
...Aye, alright. I'll find you something that needs doing. Don't make me regret it.
Hands. Good. We're short of those and long on advice.
dialogue.conversations.village.praised.a: Come to. That's the right way round — nobody arrives thinking it.
Then you've stayed long enough for it to work on you, %1$s.
Good. It takes about a winter, that. You're ahead of schedule.
The square at dusk, when the work's done and nobody's shouting yet.
That everyone knows whose child is whose. It sounds small until you've lived without it.
The well, %1$s. Not the water — the standing about it.
dialogue.conversations.village.praised.j: Then I've done my work. The mayor pays me in bread for this, you know.
We've a cottage going and a fence that wants a second pair of hands, %1$s.
Ha! Say that near the mayor and you'll be on the register by supper.
dialogue.conversations.village.respond.a: It is. Small, loud, and mine. I'd not swap it.
Aye. You'll not hear that said often, but aye.
Good of you to say. Most visitors count the mud and leave.
You've been here long enough to say that and mean it. Most agree out of politeness.
Aye — and you've seen it through a winter or two now, %1$s. Your opinion counts.
You'd know. You're not a visitor any more, whatever the rest of them say.
The well, first. Then the road. Then whoever decided where the pigs go.
Asked as though the answer mattered. ...The road, then. The road, and I'll show you where.
A dozen things. Most of them small, all of them years old.
dialogue.conversations.village.respond.i: ...It's my home, %1$s. Say that somewhere else.
Miserable. Right. And yet here you are, in it.
Everyone here has built something. You've walked through it.
dialogue.conversations.village.resume.ca: Then say so and we're square. It's the not-saying that costs people here.
Right. I'd rather a plain no now than a maybe until spring.
That's a shame and it's honest, and I'll take honest.
dialogue.conversations.village.resume.le: Do. I'll say if it changes, and I'll say plainly.
Right. It's mine to carry and it's lighter for having been said out loud.
Then it's mine again. That's how it should be, and thank you for the loan.
dialogue.conversations.village.resume.st: Then I'll stop being surprised about it and start counting on it.
Good. Half the offers this village makes are made to be remembered fondly, not kept.
I'll hold you to that, and I'll be pleasant about the holding.
dialogue.conversations.village.resume.th: You asked. People who ask get told; it isn't more complicated than that.
It costs me nothing and it seems to be worth something. I'll go on doing it.
That's the second time you've thanked me for a thing I'd have done anyway.
dialogue.conversations.village.resume.wh: Any morning that isn't market day. I'll have the tools out either way.
Before the frost, or it's a spring job and a worse one.
Whenever. I've said that to four people and none of them came, so — whenever.
dialogue.conversations.village.resume/1: That fault you said you'd put a hand to. It's still there, and so are you.
dialogue.conversations.village.resume/2: You offered to help with the wall. I've told two people you offered, which was unwise of me.
dialogue.conversations.village.resume/3: The thing you said you'd look at — I've been half expecting you and half not.
dialogue.conversations.village.settled.a: No. It isn't. Takes a while to see it that way, mind.
That's the kindest reading of 'fine' I've heard, %1$s.
Aye. Most places would trade us for it and not know what they'd got.
dialogue.conversations.village.settled.j: It is. Try telling that to anyone under twenty, mind.
A luxury. Ha. I'll use that on the next one who calls us sleepy, %1$s.
Aye. Excitement is what a village calls it afterwards, when everyone's fine.
dialogue.conversations.village.settled.p: ...The road. There, you've dragged it out of me. But it's been the road for years.
Truly. Ask me in February and you'll get a list as long as your arm, %1$s.
Nothing worth the breath. That's a strange thing to have to defend.
dialogue.conversations.village.teen/1: It's small. Everyone knows everything about everyone.
dialogue.conversations.village.teen/2: It's home. Bit quiet. That's fine, I guess.
dialogue.conversations.village.toddler.a: The bit with the water in. But I'm not allowed close.
Behind the houses. There's a gap and it's MINE.
The high bit! You can see everything from the high bit.
dialogue.conversations.village.toddler.d: It's the BEST village. There isn't a better one anywhere.
You like it too! Then you should live here. Everyone should.
dialogue.conversations.village.toddler.l: Bye! I'm going to go and be in it.
Bye bye. Don't get lost, it's big.
dialogue.conversations.village.toddler/1: I like it here! My house is here and my toys are here.
dialogue.conversations.village.toddler/2: The village is big. I'm not allowed past the well.
dialogue.conversations.village.toddler/3: This is the best village 'cause I live in it.
dialogue.conversations.village.young.ask: The well. You can shout into it.
Market day. Everyone's out and nobody's counting where I am.
The big tree. It's mine, mostly.
dialogue.conversations.village.young.pla: It IS. There's a bell and everything.
Best village. I've only seen the one, but still.
dialogue.conversations.weather.clear/1: Not a cloud up there. Days like this you forgive the place its winters.
dialogue.conversations.weather.clear/2: Clear skies and warm sun — I'd get twice the work done if I didn't keep stopping to enjoy it.
dialogue.conversations.weather.clear/3: Good clean sky today. Makes even the cracked bell and the muddy square look almost handsome.
dialogue.conversations.weather.enjoy.hig: Isn't it! I've been finding excuses to be outdoors since breakfast.
A day like this and I forget every complaint I had about this place, %1$s.
It is. Days like this are the argument for staying, and I'm having it with myself.
dialogue.conversations.weather.mild.agre: Course I am. I've been reading this sky since before you got here.
It's nice to be agreed with. Doesn't happen much around the well.
Aye. We'll be proved wrong by evening, but aye.
dialogue.conversations.weather.mild.ask_: Work, then more work, then sitting outside pretending I planned to.
Nothing grand. That's rather the luxury of a day like this.
Getting the outside jobs done before the sky changes its mind.
dialogue.conversations.weather.mild.cut_: ...It is only weather, aye. You brought it up, %1$s.
Right. I'll stop boring you with the sky, then.
dialogue.conversations.weather.mild.enjo: It is. You have to say so out loud or the good days go by unremarked.
Aye. I'll be complaining about the heat by noon, but right now — aye.
Good of you to notice it. The sky mostly gets mentioned when it's against us.
dialogue.conversations.weather.mild.grum: Would you? It's the first decent day in a fortnight, %1$s.
There's no pleasing some people. It's a lovely morning.
Mm. And now I'm looking at it differently. Thanks for that.
Ha! Finally, someone else who isn't delighted by it.
Aye, it's relentless. Nobody's allowed to say so.
Say that in the square and they'll look at you like you kicked a lamb.
Everyone wants a different sky. That's why nobody's ever happy.
Fair. It won't last either way.
You and half the village, then.
dialogue.conversations.weather.mild.leav: Aye. Get out in it while it holds.
Go on. It'll be raining by supper, mark me.
dialogue.conversations.weather.mild.talk: Every bit of it. Another week like this and the barley's made.
Ask the farmer — they'll talk your ear off. Short answer: yes.
It'll do. We wanted rain a fortnight ago; now we want exactly this.
dialogue.conversations.weather.rain/1: This rain? The crops love it even if my boots don't. We needed it, honestly.
dialogue.conversations.weather.rain/2: Grey and drizzly. Good sleeping weather, bad laundry weather. I know which I'd rather have.
dialogue.conversations.weather.rain/3: Rain again. The well's happy, the road's mud, and the frogs are showing off. Balance, I suppose.
dialogue.conversations.weather.storm.con: ...I'm alright. Wet, but alright. Kind of you to check on a day like this.
Better for being asked, %1$s. Most folk run past in this.
I've been out in worse. Still — it's nice not to be invisible in the rain.
dialogue.conversations.weather.storm.dis: Tell that to the roof. And the animals. And my nerves.
A bit of thunder took the mill's roof off two winters back, %1$s.
Easy to say from under a hood. Go and stand in it a while.
dialogue.conversations.weather.storm.jok: Some of us can't. The animals don't care what the sky's doing.
Mm. I'd rather it stopped than be funny about it.
...Right. Very restful for you, I'm sure.
Ha! It is. Best weather there is, if you've nowhere to be.
Now there's a plan. Wake me when the sky's finished shouting.
You've got the right idea and the wrong job, %1$s.
It would be, if the roof agreed.
If only. There's always something needs doing in it.
dialogue.conversations.weather.storm.lea: Aye — you get in too. Mind the road, it floods by the gate.
Go on. Don't stand under the big elm, whatever you do.
Right. Dry socks and a door between you and it, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.weather.storm.off: ...I will, actually. Thank you. It's a long storm to sit through alone.
Somewhere dry and somebody in it. That's the whole of what I wanted.
Kind of you, %1$s. I'll bring what's left of the bread.
dialogue.conversations.weather.storm.pra: The washing, if you're offering. And the small hens panic at thunder.
Shutters on the north side. They rattle loose every single time.
Now that you mention it — yes. Two hands would halve it.
dialogue.conversations.weather.storm.sta: You'd wait it out here? Alright. It's better with company.
Suit yourself — but you'll be as soaked as I am.
That's decent of you. Storms are long when you're counting alone.
dialogue.conversations.weather.storm/1: Wild sky today. I've got the shutters latched and a candle ready. Best stay in if you can, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.weather.storm/2: Thunder like that, the animals won't settle and neither will I. Mind the lightning out there.
dialogue.conversations.weather.storm/3: A proper storm. My gran said these washed the year's bad luck off the roof. I'll believe it if it lets up.
dialogue.conversations.weather.talk_crop: Not a cloud. %2$s like this is what you pray for and then immediately worry about.
It's fine growing weather, %1$s. Three more days of it and I'll start complaining about drought.
Clear sky, no wind, everything doing what it should. Suspicious, frankly.
dialogue.conversations.weather.toddler.a: The one with the pink bits at the end of the day.
Puddle sky! Best sky. You get puddles after.
Snow sky. It goes all quiet before.
dialogue.conversations.weather.toddler.l: Bye! I'm going to go look at them more.
dialogue.conversations.weather.toddler.p: YES! You SEE it! Grown-ups never look properly.
See? SEE? I told everyone and nobody listened to me.
I knew you'd get it. You're the only one who gets it, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.weather.toddler/1: Sky water! I like jumping in the puddles after.
dialogue.conversations.weather.toddler/2: The clouds look like sheep today. Big sky sheep.
dialogue.conversations.weather.toddler/3: Is it gonna thunder? I'm not scared. Maybe a little.
dialogue.conversations.work: Do you actually like your work?
dialogue.conversations.work.adventurer.r: I've been pricing roofs. Not buying one. Pricing one, which is further than I've got before.
Still the same road. I said one more and I've walked three since we spoke.
The roof got smaller in my head. That's either progress or giving up and I can't tell which.
dialogue.conversations.work.again.apolog: No harm. I like talking about it more than I let on.
You did ask, aye. My answer keeps.
It's alright, %1$s. It's the only subject I'm expert in.
dialogue.conversations.work.again.leave/: Aye. Come back when I've something new to show you.
dialogue.conversations.work.again.press/: It's the same trade it was an hour ago.
Twice? The work hasn't changed, %1$s, and neither have I.
...Fine. Same as before. Now let me get on.
dialogue.conversations.work.again/1: We covered my work already. It hasn't gotten more interesting since.
dialogue.conversations.work.again/2: The job's the same as it was this morning, %1$s. Reliable that way.
dialogue.conversations.work.again/3: Ask the work how it likes ME for a change.
dialogue.conversations.work.archer.resum: I put the second-archer request in writing. It's on the mayor's table under three other things.
No second archer. I did get one night off, which somebody covered badly.
I've found a candidate. Fifteen years old and better than I was at fifteen, which is annoying.
dialogue.conversations.work.armorer.resu: I started the suit. It's in pieces and I've already remade the left pauldron twice.
Not started. Every week something urgent turns up wearing somebody's blood.
I finished a piece of it. Somebody asked what it was for and I couldn't answer.
dialogue.conversations.work.ask_why.harv: Why? In %2$s you don't ask why. You ask whether it's in yet, and it isn't.
Ask me that in a quieter season, %1$s. Right now the answer is 'because it'll rot otherwise'.
This time of year the work does the asking and I just answer it.
dialogue.conversations.work.blunt/1: ...I would, wouldn't I. It's what you say about your own trade. ...Ask me again and I'll try harder.
dialogue.conversations.work.blunt/2: That's a rude thing to be right about, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.work.blunt/3: Hm. Fair. Half of what I say about the work is habit and the other half is defence.
dialogue.conversations.work.butcher.resu: I walked the ground for the new pens. There's a spot that would work if the smith agrees.
The pens haven't moved. I've stopped asking and started saving instead.
A child asked me what the sound was. That moved it up my list considerably.
dialogue.conversations.work.cartographer: I've a fourth description of the coast now. It contradicts the other three differently.
Nobody's taken me north yet. The map still has that guess on it and I hate looking at it.
I redrew it from scratch. It's honest now, and honest means a great deal of blank paper.
dialogue.conversations.work.child/1: My job is being a kid and I'm SO good at it.
dialogue.conversations.work.child/2: I help the grown-ups sometimes! Mostly I supervise.
dialogue.conversations.work.cleric.resum: I've a fourth candidate. She sat through an afternoon without asking once about the recipes.
No apprentice. I did the afternoons alone all season and I'm told that's my own fault.
One lasted eleven days. That's the record and I'm not sure whether to be pleased.
dialogue.conversations.work.cultist.resu: I've tested a fourth. He reached line nineteen and asked what it meant, which disqualifies him.
Nobody yet. I've started writing them down, which I said I never would.
One passed. I've told nobody, because saying it aloud would make it a succession.
I've a second pair of hands two days a week. December is now merely difficult.
Still alone in the kitchen. December went the way December goes.
I trained somebody and they left for a town kitchen. I'd have done the same.
The pot has a fund now. Small, and it is a fund, and thinning is about barley again.
Not funded. I thinned it twice this month and both times it was about people.
Two households put in without being asked. I've not stopped thinking about that.
dialogue.conversations.work.enderian.res: I showed the catalogue to the librarian. She turned three pages and asked good questions.
Still mine. Everyone who's seen it has handled it as though it might bite.
I've begun copying it, which means I've decided somebody will have it.
dialogue.conversations.work.engineer.res: The race is surveyed. Digging it is a matter of hands and a summer, which is to say money.
Not dug. The mill runs in August the way it always has, badly.
We dug forty feet of it. Forty feet is nothing, and it's forty feet more than last year.
dialogue.conversations.work.farmer.resum: I got three weeks of only the field. Three weeks, and I slept like a stone.
No such season. Fences, market, and an argument about a boundary that isn't mine.
I traded the market days away. It cost me money and I'd do it again.
dialogue.conversations.work.fisherman.re: I got as far as the headland. Not the stretch itself, but I've seen it now.
Still thinking about it more than I fish here, which the catch shows.
I asked about the boat. It'd take a fortnight and nobody to mind the nets.
dialogue.conversations.work.fletcher.res: I've a stave seasoning. It'll be two years before it's a bow, and that's the trade.
No bow. Arrows, arrows, arrows, and a winter of them ahead.
I ruined the first stave. That's apparently normal and it did not feel normal.
dialogue.conversations.work.florist.resu: I've the glass promised, secondhand, from a house that's coming down.
No glasshouse. February was February and I sold nothing for six weeks.
I built a cold frame instead. It's a tenth of the plan and it works.
dialogue.conversations.work.followup.bel: Anyone could. Nobody does. There's a difference, %1$s.
Then take the tools. Go on. I'll watch.
...Right. I'll remember that next time you need something mended.
dialogue.conversations.work.followup.hea: ...It is. Huh. Everyone else asks when it'll be finished. Right — where were we.
Wearing me down. Aye, that's the word for it. I'd not found the word.
You've been watching, then. It's the work that gets seen, not the one doing it.
dialogue.conversations.work.followup.jok: Ha. Don't tell the others. They think it holds itself up out of respect.
I am, and nobody will notice until the day I stop. That's the job, %1$s.
The reason, aye. Also the reason it breaks. Both true, sadly.
dialogue.conversations.work.followup.off: ...Huh. That'd work. Where were you three winters ago?
I've done it my way so long I stopped looking. Say it again slowly.
Not bad. I'll try it and blame you loudly if it goes wrong.
dialogue.conversations.work.generic/1: Being a %2$s isn't glamorous, but it's mine, and I'm better at it than most.
dialogue.conversations.work.generic/2: A %2$s's day starts before the sun and ends after the complaints. I'd still choose it.
dialogue.conversations.work.generic/3: Somebody in this village has to be the %2$s. Turns out somebody is me.
dialogue.conversations.work.guard.resume: There's a second guard, three nights a week. Four years is now two people's problem.
Still one guard. The wall doesn't know the difference and I do.
They gave me a candidate who's frightened of the dark. I'm working with it.
dialogue.conversations.work.hate.keep_it: It had better. Half the folk here would have an opinion and none of them useful.
Thank you. I'd rather be a grumbler than a cautionary tale, %1$s.
Good. I have watched what this place does with a man who says he wants out.
dialogue.conversations.work.hate.sympath: ...It is. Nobody's called it heavy before. They call it lucky, mostly.
Aye. And I carry it, and I'll carry it tomorrow. Thank you for calling it what it is, %1$s.
Heavy. That is the word I have been avoiding for about four years.
dialogue.conversations.work.hate.why_sta: Because the alternative is a winter I'd not survive. That's the whole romance of it.
Where would I go, %1$s? A trade is a door you walk through once.
Habit. Habit, and being good at it, which is its own kind of trap.
dialogue.conversations.work.hate/1: Between us? Some mornings I stare at the ceiling and think about just... walking.
dialogue.conversations.work.hate/2: It pays for bread. That's the nicest thing I can say about it.
dialogue.conversations.work.hate/3: Don't tell the mayor, but some days I do the whole job out of pure spite.
dialogue.conversations.work.hear_burnout: ...It is. Nobody asks the second question, and you just did. Sit down, I've things to say.
You've been watching me and not the work, %1$s. That's rarer than a good hammer.
Everything wears somebody down. That's not an insight, that's a job.
Mm. It's work, %1$s. It's supposed to be tiring.
Don't diagnose me across a workbench. I've been doing this longer than you've been watching.
Wearing me down. Right. Was that meant to be helpful?
...Aye. It is. That's the first time I've said so out loud.
It wears. You noticed. Right — back to it, but thank you.
dialogue.conversations.work.hunter.resum: The count is in the librarian's hand now. Twenty years of it, in ink that isn't mine.
Not written. I've said I'll do it every winter for six winters.
I started it and reached the third year before I had to stop for a while.
dialogue.conversations.work.hunter_exper: They're slower than me now, which is the point, and they hate it.
One left. The other is better than I was and I've not told her.
I've stopped correcting them mid-hunt. That was harder than the teaching.
dialogue.conversations.work.leatherworke: Twelve years now. The mayor has agreed in principle, which is the twelfth agreement in principle.
Not moved. I've started tanning further out instead, which costs me a mile each way.
Somebody downstream complained and it moved further in a month than in eleven years.
dialogue.conversations.work.librarian.re: The second room exists. Four people sat in it last week and nobody read a thing.
No room. The books have the space and the people stand.
I cleared a corner instead. Two chairs. It has already changed who comes in.
dialogue.conversations.work.like/1: I do, most days. There's a rhythm to it. You stop noticing the blisters.
dialogue.conversations.work.like/2: It's mine, you know? Nobody tells me how to run my own bench.
dialogue.conversations.work.like/3: Ask me at dawn and I'll grumble. Ask me when it's done and I'm proud of it.
dialogue.conversations.work.mason.resume: I've cut the voussoirs. They're stacked in the yard looking like nothing at all.
No arch. Walls, walls, a chimney, and a wall.
The centring collapsed. I'll build it again and I've learned the reason.
dialogue.conversations.work.mercenary.re: I've had an offer. Bad wage, real name, and I've not said no yet.
No post. Two contracts instead, both of which I regret differently.
I turned down a purse for a gate watch. Ask me next winter whether that was sense.
dialogue.conversations.work.miner.resume: There's a second man below twice a week now. It isn't enough and it isn't nothing.
Still alone down there. I've been careful, which is not a plan.
A boy asked to learn. I said no, and I've thought about it every day since.
dialogue.conversations.work.netherian.re: The cleric has it. She's already found two mistakes I made and hadn't noticed.
Still on my shelf. I keep deciding to hand it over on a better day.
I copied the worst chapter for her first, to see what she did with it.
dialogue.conversations.work.nitwit.resum: They gave me the well. It's a post, it has a name, and people say it out loud.
No post. I've asked twice more and been kindly not answered.
I've been minding the gate unofficially. Nobody's stopped me, which is nearly a job.
dialogue.conversations.work.none.resume/: I've been sweeping the square. Nobody asked, and now they'd notice if I stopped.
Nothing yet. The village manages without me, which is what I said I didn't want.
The mayor mentioned a post. Mentioned. I've been living on the word for a month.
dialogue.conversations.work.oceanographe: The second post is marked out. Marked out, not built, but the stakes are in.
One post still. Nineteen years is now twenty years of a single line of marks.
Somebody offered to keep the second set of readings. A stranger. I said yes too quickly.
dialogue.conversations.work.outlaw.resum: The woodworker let me hold a chisel. In daylight, where people could see.
No trade. Nobody wants to be the one seen teaching me, and I understand it.
The smith said maybe. Maybe is the best word I've had in three years.
dialogue.conversations.work.praise.high/: Ha! You've caught me on a good day and I'll take every word of that.
It has gone well, hasn't it. I'd not have said so first, but since you did, %1$s — aye!
Right you are, and don't stop there. Days like this I can take a great deal of it.
dialogue.conversations.work.praise.storm: Kind of you to say it standing out in this. Get under something.
Praise in a downpour counts double, %1$s. Now go inside.
Ha! You've picked a filthy afternoon to be complimentary. I'll take it.
dialogue.conversations.work.priest.resum: I've told one person a third of the list. They've not asked for the rest, which is right.
Still only mine. If I go tonight the list goes with me, and I know it.
I began writing it down and burned the page. It isn't a list to be written.

The saw doesn't care whose hand it is. I've two fingers that bend the wrong way to remind me.
They twisted over a winter. Two came back and one I saw in a barn, being used as a barn thing.
I bought them back and burned them, %1$s, which was expensive and correct.
Because by then your hand is tired and your eye has agreed to be satisfied. That's when frames fail.
Because the first ten decided the shape and the eleventh has to obey all of them, %1$s.
...You could. Sticks between every layer, air all the way through, and nothing touching the ground.
Do it wrong and you've made firewood out of two years of patience, %1$s. Careful.
Joints. Eleven of them for a frame, and the eleventh has to fit as well as the first did.
Seasoning stock and resisting the urge to use it early. That urge has ruined three chairs.
Nobody looks up at a beam. That's how you know it's a good one.
Wood takes a lifetime to grow and an afternoon to ruin, %1$s. I try to remember that.
They do. That's a heavier sentence than you meant it to be and I'll be carrying it all day.
Aye. Beams, doors, the table they argue across. All of it mine.
Nine. I rehang the ropes every second year and no one has asked me to.
Nine, and the fourth family brought it back for mending with an apology, %1$s. I nearly wept.
Thirty-one of thirty-four. The other three are older than me and better made, and it bothers me.
All but three. I could tell you which three from the sound they make, %1$s.
...Somebody knowing is a different thing from somebody saying. You've done the second one.
I'd assumed the not-signing meant the not-knowing followed, %1$s. Apparently not.
Every roof, every door, every table people eat at. I don't sign them and I know all of them.
I made the cradle that four families have now borrowed in turn. It's on its ninth child.
Trees give a lifetime of patience in every plank. I try to build things worthy of the wait.
I can tell any beam's tree by the grain. The tavern bar? That was a spiteful old oak. Fitting.
dialogue.conversations.work.respond.ask_: Because somebody has to, and because it's mine. That's most of it.
Why. Hm. ...Because when it's done right it lasts longer than I will. Don't repeat that.
It's the one thing in the day nobody argues with me about.
dialogue.conversations.work.respond.leav: Right you are. Mind the tools by the door.
dialogue.conversations.work.respond.prai: ...Am I? Twenty years and nobody's said it in those words. Thank you.
You'd be the first to notice. It's the joint people see, never the fitting of it.
I am, as it happens. It's good to be told once in a while, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.work.resume.ask_n: Somebody with more authority than me saying yes. That's the whole of the next step.
Money, or a season with nothing urgent in it. I've never had either at once.
Deciding it's allowed to matter. I keep putting that off and calling it prudence.
dialogue.conversations.work.resume.doubt: I did. And I'll say it next time, which is either persistence or the other thing.
That's fair, and I'd rather be told than let it become a story I tell.
So I did. Ask me again in a season and if the answer's the same, stop asking.
dialogue.conversations.work.resume.hold_: Then I'd better have a better one. That's more use to me than encouragement.
Do. Half of why nothing moves is that nobody asks twice.
Right. I'll not enjoy it and I'll be glad of it, which is how these things work.
dialogue.conversations.work.resume.no_hu: There is, a little. But thank you for saying there isn't.
That's kind and it's wrong, and I'll take the kind half.
No. There isn't. I keep forgetting that and then working through a Sunday.
dialogue.conversations.work.resume.offer: ...Say that again in a month and I'll believe you're not being polite.
Two hands and a day. That's all it is, and I've not asked anyone for a day in years.
You could ask about it in front of somebody who decides things. That's worth more than the work.
dialogue.conversations.work.scribe.resum: The second copies exist. Six of them, in the cleric's cellar, which is not stone but is not here.
No room, no copies. One fire and nineteen years of work is a rumour.
I copied the three that matter first. If it burns now we lose less than everything.
dialogue.conversations.work.shady_wizard: I said it. To a customer. She came back the next day, which I still don't understand.
Not yet. I sold certainty three times this week and slept badly each time.
I said it once and lost the sale. It felt better than the sale did.
dialogue.conversations.work.shepherd.res: Eleven fewer sheep and four of them past nine years. It's a strange sort of pride.
Same flock. The market decides these things more than I do.
I kept one back that I should have sold. That's how these plans start.
dialogue.conversations.work.teen/1: Bit of everything — whatever the grown-ups don't want to do, apparently.
dialogue.conversations.work.teen/2: Still 'finding my calling'. Today my calling was hauling firewood.
dialogue.conversations.work.toolsmith.re: I made six at the new angle. The farmer took one and hasn't complained, which is praise.
Still nonsense, apparently. I've made none, because I'd have to explain them.
I made one and used it myself all spring. My back has an opinion and it's favourable.
dialogue.conversations.work.vampire_expe: The letters are lodged with the cleric, sealed. She doesn't know what they are.
Still in my house. If it burns, four families never learn what happened.
I nearly read one again. I've moved them somewhere I can't reach easily.
I've made eleven ploughs and three swords. That ratio is new and I like it.
No ploughs. The orders come in and they're not for fields.
I made a plough and gave it away, which is not a business plan.
dialogue.conversations.work.werewolf_exp: It's written. Sealed, with the priest, and now I sleep differently.
Not written. I keep starting it and stopping at the part about the chain.
I wrote half. The half I can't write is the half that matters.
dialogue.conversations.work.woodworker.r: I've the timber for the staircase. It's stacked, and I look at it every morning.
No staircase. Doors, three doors, and a bench that needed doing.
I turned the newel post. Just that. It's on my bench like a small trophy.
dialogue.conversations.work.young.ask/1: My mother, mostly. And a lot of getting it wrong first.
dialogue.conversations.work.young.ask/2: Nobody! I watched until I worked it out.
dialogue.conversations.work.young.ask/3: The smith lets me hold things. That counts as teaching, I reckon.
dialogue.conversations.work.young.dismis: Everyone says that until they need it done.
dialogue.conversations.work.young.encour: It IS! Nobody counts it but it is.
...Thanks. Everyone calls it helping. It's work.
You get it. Grown-ups usually don't.
dialogue.conversations.work.young.leave/: Okay. I've got things to finish.
dialogue.conversations.work_offer.accept: Then let's talk properly about it.
Good. Come here and I'll lay it out.
That's settled, then. Here's the detail.
dialogue.conversations.work_offer.ask_la: Nothing today — and after the last thing you did for me, I'd almost be embarrassed to ask.
Come back tomorrow, %1$s. You've done enough for this village to be going on with.
Not just now. I'm still telling people about the last one.
dialogue.conversations.work_offer.ask_ne: Straightforward enough. I'll show you the whole of it if you're in.
Nothing heroic. It's the sort of thing that just needs doing.
More than I can manage alone, which is why I'm asking.
dialogue.conversations.work_offer.ask_te: Now that's the right question, and you're the first today to ask it before saying yes.
Terms. Good. I'd have thought less of you for not asking, %1$s.
Straight to the price. I like that. It saves us both an afternoon of politeness.
Fair question. I'd ask it too. You'll be paid properly, %1$s.
Straight to the terms. Good — I'd rather deal with someone who asks.
Whatever's fair. I'll not have it said I short anyone.
dialogue.conversations.work_offer.declin: No matter. The asking wasn't a debt.
Fair enough. It'll keep till someone's free.
Understood. Come back if that changes, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.work_offer.leave/: Take your time. It'll wait a day.
Right you are. Think on it.
dialogue.conversations.work_offer.none.a: Do. Things pile up faster than I'd like.
Aye, check back. There's always something by week's end.
I'll have something for you soon enough.
dialogue.conversations.work_offer.none.o: ...That's decent of you. There's always something, if you're offering.
Nothing paid, but I'll not turn down a spare pair of hands.
You'd help with no job in it? That's rarer than a quest, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.work_offer.refuse: There was no call for that. It was only a job.
Noted. I'll not trouble you again.
dialogue.conversations.worries.dismissed: ...Then I'll say it again, and you'll not do that twice.
Brushed off. That's the word for it, %1$s. Thank you for using it.
Alright. Quietly is no way to fret. It doubles the size of the thing.
...Perhaps not. It feels how it feels regardless, and that's the bit I live in.
That may even be true. It's a poor thing to say to somebody mid-fret, %1$s.
Then sit with me while it feels bad, and be right about it quietly.
dialogue.conversations.worries.heard.lat: That's the useful half of a promise. Everyone else only makes the other half.
I'll want more than that eventually. It's good to know where it'll be.
Then I'll ask, and I'm bad at asking, so expect it to arrive sideways.
dialogue.conversations.worries.heard.lis: ...Right. Then I'll start at the part I've not said to anybody.
You'll be here a while. I've been rehearsing this on the walk to work for a month.
Thank you. I'll not need long — I mostly needed somebody in the room.
dialogue.conversations.worries.heard/1: Yes. Everyone reaches for a solution and I've had four this week.
dialogue.conversations.worries.heard/2: I would. There's nothing to be done and being told that again would finish me.
dialogue.conversations.worries.heard/3: ...That's the first time anybody has asked instead of assuming.
dialogue.conversations.worries.informati: Would you. Then I'll stop turning it over every night until you're back.
Quietly, if you can. I'd rather the question didn't get about with my name on it.
Then that's the first useful thing anyone's offered, and I've asked four people.
...That's better than I'd feared and worse than I'd hoped. I'll take it.
Say that again slowly. I've been guessing for a fortnight on less than that.
Then I've been frightened of the wrong half of it this whole time.
It would. I don't know whether the road south is passable and I can't ask openly.
Yes. Whether it's happened to anybody else here, and whether they came out of it.
One thing. Whether the thing I'm afraid of is even possible, or I've invented it.
dialogue.conversations/1: You want to talk? Alright. What's on your mind?
dialogue.conversations/2: Sure, we can talk. What about?
dialogue.conversations/3: I'm listening. What do you want to know?
dialogue.conversations/4: Alright, you have my attention. All of it, even.
dialogue.conversations/5: Pull up a fence post. What's on your mind?
dialogue.greet.fail/6: Oh. It's you. I was hoping for the bread cart.
dialogue.greet.fail/8: If this is about the fence, I already know.
dialogue.greet.success/6: There's a face I don't mind seeing.
dialogue.greet.success/7: Morning, noon, whatever it is — good to see you, %1$s.
dialogue.greet.success/8: Well met. You picked a fine day to exist.
dialogue.greet.success/9: Ah, %1$s! I was just thinking the day needed improving.
dialogue.main/11: You've got that look. What is it this time?
dialogue.main/12: Talk to me. The turnips can wait.
dialogue.main/9: I've got a few minutes before someone needs something.
dialogue.mcareputation.gossip.project_co: We'd never have finished %3$s without %2$s. That's just the truth of it.
dialogue.mcareputation.gossip.project_fa: %3$s came to nothing in the end. %2$s tried, I'll grant that much.
dialogue.mcareputation.gossip.project_ph: %2$s has been putting real hours into %3$s. It shows.
dialogue.mcareputation.gossip.promise_br: %2$s gave %3$s their word once. For all that was worth.
dialogue.mcareputation.gossip.promise_ke: %2$s gave %3$s their word and kept it. Rarer than it ought to be.
dialogue.mcareputation.gossip.public_apo: You heard %2$s say sorry to %3$s in front of everyone? Takes something, that.
dialogue.mcareputation.gossip.quest_aban: %2$s just walked away from %3$s, you know. Half-done and left.
dialogue.mcareputation.gossip.quest_comp: Credit where it's due — %2$s did what they said they would about %3$s.
%3$s got sorted, and it was %2$s who sorted it. Word gets around.
dialogue.mcareputation.gossip.quest_fail: %2$s never did see %3$s through. People noticed.
dialogue.mcareputation.gossip.restitutio: %2$s put things right with %3$s in the end. That counts for plenty around here.
dialogue.mcareputation.gossip.situation_: When %3$s had us all worried, it was %2$s who saw it through.
dialogue.mcareputation.gossip.villager_a: I'll say it plain, since you're asking: %2$s raised a hand to %3$s. Folk don't forget that quickly.
There was that business with %3$s. %2$s struck them, in the open. It got talked about.
dialogue.mcareputation.gossip.villager_k: Everyone here knows what %2$s did to %3$s. Killed them. That's not gossip, that's grief.
We buried %3$s because of %2$s. Nobody's pretending otherwise.
dialogue.shake_hand.success/6: Firm grip! You'd survive market day.
dialogue.shake_hand.success/7: A proper handshake. Rarer than emeralds these days.
dialogue.shake_hand.success/8: Deal's a deal, whatever we just agreed to.
dialogue.story.success/10: One more? Alright — the year the river froze solid, we bowled with pumpkins on it.
dialogue.story.success/11: Did I tell you about the trader who sold maps to places he invented? Half the village still owns one.
dialogue.story.success/12: There was a rooster here once so mean it had its own warning sign. True story.
dialogue.story.success/13: My grandmother could predict rain with her knees. Never wrong. Terrifying woman.
